title: Medicine Hat College Student Awards
audience: Students starting or continuing at Medicine Hat College
notes: MHC's own award page says applications for the next round open March 1, 2027 and does not publish a closing date. It also does not publish individual award amounts, which is why this shows a range rather than a figure.
description: Medicine Hat College hands out more than $400,000 a year in scholarships and bursaries to new, continuing and returning students. Some are marked on grades, some on financial need, and many on both. One online form enters you for every award you qualify for, so you do not apply to them individually.
metaDetail: One form enters you for every award you qualify for.

title: South Country Co-op Scholarship
audience: High school students in the South Country Co-op trading area
notes: The Co-op's page sets the deadline as July 31 of each year, so this repeats annually. Your family has to be a member in good standing and have bought at least $2,000 from the Co-op in the current fiscal year, so check with whoever holds the membership before you write the essay.
description: South Country Co-op gives $1,000 to a student from a member family graduating from a high school in its trading area. You need proof of acceptance and paid registration at a post-secondary institution, a 500 word essay on your community involvement, and two or more reference letters about it.
metaDetail: Your family needs a Co-op membership in good standing.

title: Alberta Indigenous Careers Award
audience: Indigenous students enrolled full-time at an Alberta post-secondary school
notes: Apply through the Student Awards office at your post-secondary school. Deadlines vary by school, so ask as soon as you have your acceptance.
description: Worth $2,000 per term and up to $4,000 an academic year for Indigenous students enrolled full-time in a certificate, diploma, applied degree or bachelor program in Alberta. You need at least a 60 percent course load, or 40 percent with a documented disability, and satisfactory academic standing.
metaDetail: Apply through your post-secondary Student Awards office.

title: RE/MAX Quest for Excellence
audience: Graduating high school students demonstrating leadership
notes: Dates confirmed against RE/MAX's own Official Rules on 2026-08-07: the program opens August 24, 2026 and closes March 15, 2027. The old /quest-for-excellence/ landing page 404s between cycles, so this points at the rules page, which stays up year-round.
description: RE/MAX gives $1,000 to graduating students in the Medicine Hat region heading to post-secondary, with selection weighted toward leadership.

title: Alexander Rutherford Scholarship
audience: Alberta high school students based on academic averages
description: Alberta's flagship high school scholarship, worth up to $2,500 depending on your averages in Grades 10 through 12. If you only apply for one thing on this site, apply for this.
metaDetail: Applications open August 1 with no closing deadline.
notes: Alberta Student Aid names Lloydminster as a border community: all students living there are eligible, whether the Alberta side or the Saskatchewan side, provided they attend Holy Rosary High School or Lloydminster Comprehensive High School. Your courses still have to line up with the Alberta curriculum, so ask about your transcript early.

title: Cypress County Agricultural Service Board Bursary
audience: Students entering an agriculture related program at a college or university
notes: The County's page sets the deadline at September 30 each year, not the spring date this listing carried before. Two bursaries are available per calendar year. The same page also points at the separate AAAF Memorial Bursary for agricultural or environmental science students, which is run provincially.
description: Cypress County awards two $1,000 bursaries a year to students carrying on to a college or university in an agriculture related program. Applications and supporting documents go to the County's Agricultural Supervisor.
metaDetail: Two are awarded each calendar year.

title: Servus Credit Union Young Adult Scholarship
audience: Servus Credit Union members entering post-secondary
notes: The link goes to the Servus home page because Servus does not keep a standing scholarship page. Ask your counsellor or your local branch whether this is running before you plan on it.
description: Servus Credit Union offers this $1,500 scholarship to support members who are entering post-secondary education. Applicants must be Servus Credit Union members in good standing. Contact your school guidance counsellor for application details.

title: ATB Financial Bursary
audience: Indigenous students from Alberta in or heading into post-secondary
notes: Part of Indspire's Building Brighter Futures. One application covers every Indspire award you qualify for, and it stays in the running for all three cutoffs: August 1, November 1 and February 1 at 11:59 p.m. EST. Apply at indspire.microsoftcrmportals.com and use one account only.
description: ATB Financial funds Indigenous students at colleges, universities, technical colleges and apprenticeship programs across Canada. Demonstrated financial need is the main thing they weigh, then community involvement and academic record. First preference goes to Alberta students entering finance, commerce, technology or Indigenous studies, but other programs are eligible. Indspire does not publish a set dollar amount for this one.

title: ATA Local 21 Scholarship
audience: Children of Elk Island Catholic Schools teachers (Sherwood Park, Fort Saskatchewan, Camrose, Vegreville area)
notes: The board here is the parent's employer, not the school you attend, so you qualify wherever you go to school. Administered through your school, so the date shown is last cycle rolled forward. Ask your counsellor for this year's date as soon as school starts.
description: A $1,000 scholarship from Alberta Teachers' Association Local 21, only for children of Elk Island Catholic Schools staff in the Sherwood Park, Fort Saskatchewan, Camrose, and Vegreville areas. Awarded on academic standing.

title: Southeastern Alberta Regional Science Fair Award
audience: Top senior projects at the SEAR Science Fair
description: Senior-division projects (grades 11-12) at the Southeast Alberta Regional Science Fair compete for certificates, prizes and special awards, and up to five seniors advance to the Canada Wide Science Fair with expenses paid.
notes: Praxis has confirmed the 2027 Southeastern Alberta Regional Science Fair for March 20, 2027 at Medicine Hat College. The date here is the fair itself; registration closes earlier, so watch the Praxis page. Prizes range from certificates to national level awards and university scholarships, which is why no single amount is listed.

title: Belcourt Brosseau Métis Awards
audience: Métis students from Alberta entering or continuing post-secondary
notes: Applications open January 2 and close March 31 at 6:00 p.m. You need proof of Métis citizenship or membership, or a letter confirming your application for it is in progress.
description: The Belcourt Brosseau Métis Awards pay between $1,000 and $10,000 a year and have put more than $12 million toward roughly 3,900 Métis students over two decades, which makes them one of the largest non-governmental funders of Métis students in Canada. You need citizenship with the Otipemisiwak Métis Government or membership in a Métis Settlement, Alberta residency, Canadian citizenship, and a place in an eligible program at an eligible post-secondary school.

title: Kermet Archibald & Jacoba Van den Brink Entrance Bursary
audience: Grade 12 CBE and Calgary Catholic students in sciences or designated trades
notes: Administered by EducationMatters through one application for all CBE and Calgary Catholic awards. Applications open March 1; most close May 30, a few May 1. Confirm this award's own deadline in the portal before you rely on the date here.
description: $10,000 in year one, renewable up to three more years at $6,500, for hard sciences, engineering, geology, biology, veterinary medicine or health sciences. A trades and vocational stream is worth $15,000 in total. Financial need and a 500-word essay required.
metaDetail: Hard sciences or a designated trade, renewable for four years.

title: Marguerite Patricia P. Bannister Memorial Degree Awards
audience: Graduating Calgary CBE/CCSD high school students entering University of Calgary
notes: The provider had not posted a date for the new cycle when this was checked in August 2026, so this is last cycle's deadline rolled forward. Confirm before you plan around it.
description: This $4,000 award honors the legacy of Marguerite Patricia P. Bannister by supporting graduating high school students from Calgary's CBE and CCSD schools who are entering the University of Calgary. The scholarship recognizes academic achievement and assists students as they transition to university-level studies.

title: Bill Gibson Bursary
audience: Graduating Calgary-area high school student entering post-secondary
notes: The provider had not posted a date for the new cycle when this was checked in August 2026, so this is last cycle's deadline rolled forward. Confirm before you plan around it.
description: A $10,000 bursary for graduating Calgary-area students entering post-secondary studies.

title: Optimist Club William J. Cummer Scholarship
audience: Alberta students entering the final year of a first undergraduate certificate, degree or diploma
notes: This listing previously showed as a Grade 12 award. The Calgary Foundation page is explicit that applicants must be entering their final year of study, so it is filed here as a post-secondary award. It is worth knowing about in Grade 12 anyway, because you can come back to it. The provider had not posted a date for the new cycle when this was checked in August 2026, so this is last cycle's deadline rolled forward. Confirm before you plan around it.
description: One award of about $2,500 with smaller awards possible, from the Optimist Club of Calgary. It is not an entrance award: you must already be enrolled at a Canadian post-secondary institution and entering the final year of your first certificate, degree or diploma. Preference goes to students from the Calgary area.

title: Calgary Flames Foundation Community Involvement Scholarship
audience: Grade 12 CBE and Calgary Catholic students with volunteer records
notes: Administered by EducationMatters through one application for all CBE and Calgary Catholic awards. Applications open March 1; most close May 30, a few May 1. Confirm this award's own deadline in the portal before you rely on the date here.
description: Four awards a year for students who show leadership through volunteering in their school or community. Essay and one reference letter required.
metaDetail: Four a year, on volunteering and one reference.

title: Edith Berger Memorial Scholarship
audience: Grade 12 CBE and Calgary Catholic students entering teaching
notes: Administered by EducationMatters through one application for all CBE and Calgary Catholic awards. Applications open March 1; most close May 30, a few May 1. Confirm this award's own deadline in the portal before you rely on the date here.
description: For a student heading into post-secondary studies to become a teacher, with a 70 percent minimum average.
metaDetail: For students on the path to becoming a teacher.

title: Big Brothers Big Sisters Society of Calgary and Area Scholarship
audience: Grade 12 CBE and Calgary Catholic students involved with Big Brothers Big Sisters
notes: Administered by EducationMatters through one application for all CBE and Calgary Catholic awards. Applications open March 1; most close May 30, a few May 1. Confirm this award's own deadline in the portal before you rely on the date here.
description: For a student with past or present involvement in Big Brothers Big Sisters of Calgary and Area.
metaDetail: Community involvement counts, and so does mentorship experience.

title: Eimer Scholarship Fund Award for Health Care
audience: Grade 12 CBE and Calgary Catholic students entering health care
notes: Administered by EducationMatters through one application for all CBE and Calgary Catholic awards. Applications open March 1; most close May 30, a few May 1. Confirm this award's own deadline in the portal before you rely on the date here.
description: Up to ten awards for students entering their first year of a practical health care program at Bow Valley College, Mount Royal University, SAIT or the University of Calgary.
metaDetail: Bow Valley, Mount Royal, SAIT or the U of C.

title: Alex Tutschek FCPA, FCA Award for Indigenous Student High School Achievement
audience: Grade 12 Indigenous Albertans accepted into an Alberta business program
notes: Apply through the online form on the CPA Education Foundation site, one form per award. CPA has not published the 2027 dates yet. May 1 has been the deadline in recent years, so confirm with cpaef@cpaalberta.ca before you count on it.
description: Two $1,500 awards for Grade 12 Indigenous students who are enrolled in or accepted into a business program at an Alberta college, polytechnic or university that offers the prerequisites for the CPA Professional Education Program. You have to be an Alberta resident, self-identify as First Nations (status or non-status), Métis or Inuit, and submit a letter or a two to three minute video on why you are heading into business or accounting, plus recent transcripts and one letter of support from an instructor. Preference goes to students who intend to pursue the CPA designation.

title: CPA Alberta Young Emerging Professional Award
audience: Grade 12 Alberta students demonstrating professionalism, integrity, and leadership
notes: Apply through the online form on the CPA Education Foundation site, one form per award. CPA has not published the 2027 dates yet. May 1 has been the deadline in recent years, so confirm with cpaef@cpaalberta.ca before you count on it.
description: Two $1,500 awards for Alberta high school students, judged on professionalism, integrity, ethics and leadership on top of satisfactory academic standing. You submit a letter or a two to three minute video on the qualities that make a successful business leader, recent transcripts, a letter from a teacher and a second letter from someone who is not a teacher or family member. Preference goes to students interested in the CPA designation.

title: David Bentley FCPA FCA and Janet Bentley High School Excellence Award
audience: Grade 12 Albertans, preference for those relocating within Alberta for post-secondary
notes: Apply through the online form on the CPA Education Foundation site, one form per award. CPA has not published the 2027 dates yet. May 1 has been the deadline in recent years, so confirm with cpaef@cpaalberta.ca before you count on it.
description: One $2,500 award for a Grade 12 student at any Alberta high school, based on volunteer involvement, satisfactory academic achievement and a stated interest in a professional accounting designation. Your application letter needs to indicate financial need. You must have finished Grades 10 and 11 in Alberta and provide proof of acceptance at an Alberta post-secondary. Preference goes to applicants who have to relocate within Alberta to attend, and to those living outside the major cities.

title: Empowered Young Woman Award
audience: Grade 12 Alberta students who identify as a girl or woman
notes: Apply through the online form on the CPA Education Foundation site, one form per award. CPA has not published the 2027 dates yet. May 1 has been the deadline in recent years, so confirm with cpaef@cpaalberta.ca before you count on it.
description: One $2,000 award from the CPA Education Foundation for a Grade 12 Alberta student who identifies as a girl or woman, judged on good character and leadership rather than marks. You submit a letter or a two to three minute video on what being an empowered young woman means to you, your post-secondary acceptance letter, and one letter of support that speaks to your character and any obstacles you have had to get past. Preference goes to students interested in the CPA designation.
metaDetail: Judged on character and leadership rather than marks.

title: Kelly & Creaghan Stepping Up in the Community Award
audience: Grade 12 Alberta students who demonstrate leadership through volunteering
notes: Apply through the online form on the CPA Education Foundation site, one form per award. CPA has not published the 2027 dates yet. May 1 has been the deadline in recent years, so confirm with cpaef@cpaalberta.ca before you count on it.
description: One $2,000 award for a Grade 12 Albertan with a real volunteer record at school or in the community. You submit a letter or a two to three minute video on a volunteer activity you actually do and what giving back has done for you, your post-secondary acceptance letter, and one letter of support. Preference goes to students interested in the CPA designation.

title: Michael Burnyeat FCPA, FCA Sparking Great Careers High School Award
audience: Grade 12 Alberta students entering BBA, B.Mgmt, or B.Comm at an Alberta institution
notes: Apply through the online form on the CPA Education Foundation site, one form per award. CPA has not published the 2027 dates yet. May 1 has been the deadline in recent years, so confirm with cpaef@cpaalberta.ca before you count on it.
description: Four $1,250 awards for Grade 12 students at Alberta high schools who have been accepted into a Bachelor of Business Administration, Bachelor of Management or Bachelor of Commerce program at an Alberta post-secondary. Your letter has to indicate financial need, show professionalism, integrity, ethics and leadership, and state that you have no immediate family member who is a CPA. You also need proof of acceptance and at least one letter of support from a teacher or community leader.

title: Horatio Alger Association of Canada Scholarship
audience: Grade 11 students across Canada (Grade 12 in Québec)
description: Horatio Alger Canada funds students who have come through real adversity. You need a family income under $65,000, at least a 65% average, and a story of pushing through hard circumstances. Open to graduating seniors across Canada.
metaDetail: Needs a family income under $65,000 and a 65% average.
notes: Applies in Grade 11, not Grade 12. There are 160 awards of $10,000, and the window is January 1 to March 31. Household net income must be $80,000 or less. Québec CEGEP students apply on a separate later deadline.

title: WorldSkills Provincial Champion Scholarship
audience: Top 2 Grade 12 podium finishers at the Provincial Skills Canada Competition
notes: No fixed deadline. You qualify by finishing on the podium at the Provincial Skills Canada Competition, then send Alberta Student Aid the application form and your Skills Canada Alberta letter of endorsement. You have two years from the date of the letter to claim it.
description: $1,200 from the Alberta Heritage Scholarship Fund for a top podium finish at the Provincial Skills Canada Competition. It goes to the top two Grade 12 finishers and the top post-secondary finisher. You have to be a Canadian citizen, permanent resident or protected person, and an Alberta resident. Visa students are not eligible.

title: First Nations, Métis and Inuit Bursary
audience: Indigenous students in full-time post-secondary, with return of service in northern Alberta
notes: Two intakes each year: February 1 to June 1, and June 5 to November 1. Apply in one intake only, late applications are not accepted. You need a verified Alberta.ca Account, which can take up to two weeks to set up.
description: Up to $11,500 a year for First Nations, Métis and Inuit students in a degree program, or up to $7,000 for a certificate, diploma or pre-apprenticeship program. In exchange you sign a return of service agreement: one year of full-time work in northern Alberta for each year of funding. You reapply every year, to a maximum of four.

title: New Beginnings Bursary
audience: Alberta students who qualify for full-time student aid and enrol in an eligible high-demand program
notes: There is no separate application. Recipients are picked from full-time Alberta Student Aid applications on a first come, first served basis, so apply for student aid as early as you can. Lifetime maximum of two bursaries.
description: A $5,000 bursary for students from low-income families who qualify for full-time Alberta Student Aid and enrol in an approved high-demand program. Alberta expanded it for 2026-27: 2,400 bursaries instead of 1,000, a $12 million budget, and more eligible programs in technology, health and energy. You do not apply separately, so get your student aid application in early.

title: Loran Scholarship
audience: Canadian citizens or permanent residents entering university for the first time in 2027, with an 88% average
description: Canada's largest undergraduate merit award, worth approximately $150,000 over four years: a $12,000 annual stipend, a full tuition waiver at a partner university, and up to $14,000 for summer programs. Selection weighs character and service as heavily as marks, over online semi-finals and national interviews in Toronto.
notes: You apply directly at apply.loranscholar.ca; the 88% is calculated from Grade 10, 11 and 12 courses only. Applicants must be born between January 1, 2005 and September 1, 2011. Even if you do not make the final class, up to 54 finalists receive $6,000 and up to 70 provincial and territorial recipients receive $3,000.
metaDetail: Applications close at noon ET.

title: Schulich Leader Scholarships
audience: Canadian high school students entering STEM at one of 20 selected universities; school nominates 1 student
notes: Your school nominates you, you cannot apply directly. Every Canadian high school can put forward one graduating student, two if the school had a Schulich Leader in 2026. Nomination deadline is January 27, 2027 and nominated students then have until February 17, 2027 to submit the application and reference letters. Talk to your counsellor in the fall, not in January.
description: The Schulich Leader Scholarships recognize exceptional Canadian high school students pursuing STEM at one of 20 select Canadian universities. Recipients are nominated by their school and receive $100,000 to support their post-secondary education. Eligible students must be graduating high school seniors planning to enter a STEM program at a participating institution.

title: TD Scholarships for Community Leadership
audience: Canadian students with 75%+ GPA and significant community involvement
description: TD's community leadership scholarship pays up to $70,000 to graduating Canadian students with at least a 75% average and a serious record of community work. One of the few big awards where what you've done matters more than your marks.

title: Terry Fox Humanitarian Award
audience: Canadian students demonstrating humanitarian work, up to 4 years of funding
notes: Heads up: the Terry Fox Humanitarian Award had not posted the next cycle date when this was checked in August 2026, so this is last year's date rolled forward. Confirm on their site before you plan around it.
description: Up to $28,000 over four years for Canadian students with a sustained record of humanitarian work. The selection committee looks for years of service, not a single project.

title: Advancing Futures Bursary
audience: Alberta youth aged 18–24 who have been in government care (foster care) at any point
notes: Three deadlines a year, tied to when you start school: apply by June 1 to start September to December, October 1 to start January to April, February 1 to start May to August. The next one is October 1, 2026. You reapply every year.
description: Alberta pays up to $40,000 toward post-secondary for youth aged 18 to 24 who have been in government care. If you've been in foster care, this is the largest source of funding available to you in the province.

title: UCalgary Pathways to Medicine Scholarship
audience: High school students applying to University of Calgary undergraduate programs
notes: Applications open October 1, 2026 and close December 1. Shortlisted applicants get a preliminary application in early December, due early January, with decisions in February.
description: UCalgary's renewable award for low-income, rural, and Indigenous students entering its undergraduate programs: up to $5,000 a year, to a maximum of $20,000 over four years, with an eye toward students headed for medicine.

title: Keyera Energy: Peter J. Renton Memorial Scholarship
audience: Alberta residents entering first year of an oil & gas related degree or diploma at an AB institution
notes: Open August 1 to October 31 each year. Two awards of $3,000. Preference goes to the previous year's recipients if they hold a 3.0 GPA. You submit an essay on your community service, work, leadership and marks, and how your field connects to the energy sector.
description: Keyera's $6,000 scholarship, in memory of Peter J. Renton, goes to a graduating Albertan starting an oil and gas related degree or diploma at an Alberta institution.

title: NADC Northern Alberta Development Council Bursary
audience: Students in the final two years of a post-secondary program, with return of service in northern Alberta
notes: Applications are accepted January 2 to May 15 each year for fall enrolment. Decisions go out by the end of July. You need a verified Alberta.ca Account, which can take up to two weeks to set up.
description: Up to $7,000 a year, for a maximum of two years, for students training for jobs northern Alberta needs. You commit to one year of full-time work in northern Alberta for each year of funding you receive. You must be 18 or older, an Alberta resident for the past 12 months, and in the last two years of your program.

title: Premier's Citizenship Award
audience: Alberta high school students; each school nominates ONE student per year
notes: The 2027 intake opens March 1, 2027. Your school nominates you, one graduating Grade 12 student per Alberta high school, and you have to hold this nomination before you can apply for the Alberta Centennial or Queen Elizabeth II Platinum Jubilee awards. Submitted through the GATE Front Office system.
description: The Premier's Citizenship Award recognizes Alberta high school students who demonstrate exceptional commitment to their communities. Each school nominates one graduating student annually to receive this $7,005 award in recognition of their citizenship and community contributions.

title: Calgary Stampede Grade 12 Western Art Scholarship
audience: Southern Alberta Grade 12 students who create western art
notes: Six scholarships: three for students at Calgary high schools and three for students elsewhere in southern Alberta. The Stampede does not post the deadline, so this is last cycle rolled forward. Email stampedescholarshipart@gmail.com to confirm.
description: The Calgary Stampede gives $2,000 to a Grade 12 student in Southern Alberta for western art: work rooted in the culture and traditions of the Canadian West.

title: ASAA Alberta Milk Scholarship
audience: Grade 12 ASAA member school students; school nominates 1 male + 1 female student
notes: Deadline is April 29 every year. You have to be registered at a School Sport Alberta member school, take part in athletics, and be heading into post-secondary.
description: The ASAA Alberta Milk Scholarship recognizes academic achievement among high school students in Alberta. One male and one female student from ASAA member schools are nominated and awarded $1,000 each by their schools.

title: Anna & John Kolesar Memorial Scholarship
audience: Alberta grads entering a Faculty of Education, with no parent holding a university degree
notes: Open August 1 to October 31 each year. You submit the form to Alberta Student Aid, and the money is released once they confirm you are enrolled full time in a Faculty of Education.
description: One award of $1,500 from the Alberta Heritage Scholarship Fund for a student graduating from an Alberta high school this year and heading into a Faculty of Education full time at an Alberta public post-secondary. The catch that rules most people out, and lets others in: neither of your parents can hold a university degree. You also have to be a Canadian citizen, permanent resident or protected person, and an Alberta resident. Visa students are not eligible.

title: IODE Coronation Bursary
audience: Alberta high school students entering any degree program in AB, 3+ years AB resident, financial need
notes: IODE lists the value inconsistently, as two bursaries of $1,000 and also as $5,000 awarded one per year as funds allow. The application is a Word document you download from the IODE page. Confirm the amount and the deadline with IODE Alberta before applying.
description: The IODE (Imperial Order Daughters of the Empire) Coronation Bursary supports Alberta high school students who demonstrate financial need and plan to pursue any degree program at an Alberta post-secondary institution. Applicants must have been Alberta residents for at least three years. This $1,000 bursary helps make higher education more accessible for deserving students.

title: Canadian Natural Resources Scholarship
audience: Dependents of Canadian Natural employees, or Indigenous students from communities near its operations, already enrolled in post-secondary or trade school
description: Canadian Natural's Building Futures program supports western Canadian students already enrolled in post-secondary or trade school, with a 2.5 GPA minimum. Eligibility is limited to children and dependents of employees and to Indigenous students from communities near company operations, and it favours fields relevant to oil and gas. Applications run November 10 to December 15.

title: Bayer Fund Opportunity Scholarship
audience: Canadian final-year high school students entering agriculture, food science, or culinary programs
notes: Worth checking before you spend time on it: the Bayer Fund application portal still shows 2019-2020 wording, so the Canadian high school stream may no longer be running. 4-H Alberta lists a live Bayer scholarship with a May 1 or June 1 deadline, which may be the current route.
description: The Bayer Fund's $1,500 award for Canadian graduates entering agriculture, food science, or culinary programs.

title: Dr. Ernest and Minnie Mehl Scholarship
audience: Alberta students; automatically considered when applying for the Alexander Rutherford Scholarship
description: The Dr. Ernest and Minnie Mehl Scholarship is an Alberta-based academic award of $3,500 for high school students preparing to enter post-secondary education. Students are automatically considered for this scholarship when applying for the Alexander Rutherford Scholarship, making it part of Alberta's broader support for academic achievement.

title: Catherine and Robert Povaschuk Scholarship
audience: Edmonton Public Schools Grade 12 students with honours standing, conditional acceptance to UofA
notes: Edmonton Public Schools Foundation says applications for the 2026-27 award open in February 2027. It has not posted the closing date yet, so the date shown is last cycle rolled forward. Recipients are contacted in June.
description: $1,500 for an Edmonton Public Schools Grade 12 student with honours standing and conditional acceptance to the University of Alberta.

title: Betty Finch Scholarship
audience: Edmonton Public Schools Grade 12 students with a learning disability
notes: Edmonton Public Schools Foundation says applications for the 2026-27 award open in February 2027. It has not posted the closing date yet, so the date shown is last cycle rolled forward. Recipients are contacted in June.
description: Up to $4,000 for a graduating Edmonton Public Schools student who has, or had, a diagnosed learning disability or received specialized supports for one, and needs financial help to take up a post-secondary place they have already been conditionally offered.

title: Esther and Peter Cunliffe Scholarship
audience: Edmonton Public Schools Grade 12 students headed to UofA, NAIT or MacEwan
notes: Edmonton Public Schools Foundation says applications for the 2026-27 award open in February 2027. It has not posted the closing date yet, so the date shown is last cycle rolled forward. Recipients are contacted in June.
description: $3,000 for a graduating Edmonton Public Schools student with excellent academic performance and strong personal and leadership qualities, who needs financial support and holds conditional acceptance at the University of Alberta, NAIT or MacEwan University.

title: Grace Elaine Campbell Scholarship
audience: Edmonton Public Schools Grade 12 students who attended Garneau School
notes: Edmonton Public Schools Foundation says applications for the 2026-27 award open in February 2027. It has not posted the closing date yet, so the date shown is last cycle rolled forward. Recipients are contacted in June.
description: $500 for a graduating Edmonton Public Schools student who attended Garneau School in Edmonton for at least two years and earned a final blended mark of 50 per cent or higher in English 30-1 or 30-2. The highest English 30-2 mark among qualifying students wins.

title: James P. Jones Scholarship
audience: Edmonton Public Schools Grade 12 students taking 30-level French
notes: Edmonton Public Schools Foundation says applications for the 2026-27 award open in February 2027. It has not posted the closing date yet, so the date shown is last cycle rolled forward. Recipients are contacted in June.
description: $600 for a graduating Edmonton Public Schools student taking 30-level French who shows excellent academic performance and citizenship and intends to keep studying French after high school. Shortlisted applicants do an oral interview and a written assignment, both in French.
metaDetail: Selection includes an interview in French.

title: Sandra B. Woitas Opportunity Through Education Scholarship
audience: Edmonton Public Schools Grade 12 students demonstrating educational commitment
notes: Edmonton Public Schools Foundation says applications for the 2026-27 award open in February 2027. It has not posted the closing date yet, so the date shown is last cycle rolled forward. Recipients are contacted in June.
description: $1,000 through the Edmonton Public Schools community for a Grade 12 student whose record shows genuine commitment to their education.

title: LeRoy Warden & Associates Scholarship
audience: Edmonton Public Schools Grade 12 students with financial need and clear career plans
notes: Edmonton Public Schools Foundation says applications for the 2026-27 award open in February 2027. It has not posted the closing date yet, so the date shown is last cycle rolled forward. Recipients are contacted in June.
description: Covers fall and winter tuition and mandatory fees, to a maximum of $10,000, for a graduating Edmonton Public Schools student with clear career plans and financial need holding conditional acceptance at the University of Alberta, MacEwan, NAIT or Campus Saint-Jean. Paid straight to the institution, and it does not cover books, application fees or tuition deposits.

title: Winspear Fund Scholarships for Classical Music
audience: Students in Edmonton or Northern Alberta pursuing advanced classical music study
notes: Opens January 15 and closes March 31 at 4:30 p.m. Several awards are given, from $2,000 to $10,000, and the number varies year to year. You need a reference letter from your current major teacher. Decisions come around mid-June.
description: Winspear Fund money for advanced classical music study, open to students from Edmonton and Northern Alberta. A serious performance background is expected.

title: Ranald and Vera Shean Memorial Scholarships
audience: Students age 12+ in Edmonton or Northern Alberta pursuing violin or piano study
notes: Opens January 15 and closes March 31 at 4:30 p.m. Several awards from $2,000 to $8,000, with the number varying year to year. Decisions come in early June.
description: The Shean Memorial awards, worth $8,000, go to violin and piano students aged 12 and older in Edmonton and Northern Alberta with a serious classical background.

title: Mah Society of Edmonton Centennial Scholarship
audience: Students with the surname "Mah" entering post-secondary in Canada
notes: The 2026 round closed April 17. The Mah Society has not posted 2027 dates, so this is rolled forward. Applications go to Gene Mah at mahsocietyedmonton@gmail.com.
description: The Mah Society of Edmonton gives $1,000 to a student entering post-secondary anywhere in Canada who carries the surname Mah. That is the whole requirement: any background, no minimum average.

title: Don and Norine Lowry Awards for Women of Excellence
audience: Women resident in the City of Edmonton studying energy, power, water, business, technology, safety or healthcare
notes: Edmonton Community Foundation does not publish the award value, so plan around the criteria rather than a number. Applications open March 31 and close May 31 at 4:30 p.m., with decisions in late July.
description: For women living in the City of Edmonton who are pursuing energy, power, water, business administration, finance, safety, information technology, emergency management, communications or healthcare at a public post-secondary institution operating in Edmonton. Surrounding municipalities are not eligible.

title: Lethbridge School Division ICE Scholarship
audience: Lethbridge School Division students demonstrating innovation, creativity, and entrepreneurship
notes: The 2026 application period ran January 13 to April 29. Lethbridge School Division has not posted 2027 dates, so these are rolled forward.
description: Lethbridge School Division's ICE award (innovation, creativity, entrepreneurship) pays $2,500 to a division student who shows initiative and original problem-solving.

title: Lethbridge County Community Benefit Scholarship
audience: High school students in Lethbridge County area entering STEM programs
notes: Two scholarships of $2,000, deadline June 1. The county runs this with the Stirling Wind Project and some lists name it the Stirling Wind Project Community Benefit Scholarship, so do not apply twice thinking they are separate awards. Lethbridge County also runs a separate Community Benefit Fund for organizations, which closes March 1 and is not a student award.
description: The Lethbridge County Community Benefit Scholarship supports high school students in the Lethbridge County area who are pursuing post-secondary studies in STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics) fields. This $2,000 award recognizes academic achievement and commitment to science and technology education. Students must be graduating from a Lethbridge County high school and planning to enter a STEM program at a post-secondary institution.

title: University of Lethbridge Board of Governors Award
audience: Grade 12 students applying to University of Lethbridge; automatic consideration with admission application
description: The University of Lethbridge Board of Governors Award provides $1,000 to Grade 12 students pursuing post-secondary education. Students applying to the University of Lethbridge are automatically considered for this award based on their admission application, with no separate application process required.

title: University of Lethbridge Grade 11 Merit Award
audience: Grade 11 students planning to attend ULethbridge; 75% average and above
notes: You submit the online form before June 30 of your Grade 11 year, and the award is calculated from your Grade 11 average. Grade 12 students should look at the Board of Governors admission scholarship instead, which runs off the December 15 early admission deadline.
description: The University of Lethbridge awards this $800 merit scholarship to Grade 11 students who demonstrate strong academic performance and plan to attend ULethbridge for post-secondary studies. To qualify, students must maintain a 75% average or above.

title: LaDue Ladies Lunch Scholarship
audience: Female-identifying Grade 12 students in Alberta entering post-secondary
notes: The 2026 round opened January 26 and closed at midnight April 17. These are those dates rolled forward, so check ladueladieslunch.ca in January.
description: The LaDue Ladies Lunch Scholarship supports female-identifying Grade 12 students in Alberta who are entering post-secondary education. This $4,000 award recognizes and encourages young women pursuing their educational goals at the post-secondary level.

title: Bette Joan Rac Piano Scholarship
audience: Piano students in Alberta
notes: Deadline is April 30 every year. One $1,000 award, presented annually through the Alberta Piano Teachers Association.
description: This $1,000 scholarship supports piano students pursuing their musical education in Alberta. Offered to recognize excellence and passion in piano performance, it is open to high school students interested in continuing their musical studies.
metaDetail: Recognizes excellence and passion in piano performance.

title: Hec Gervais Academic and Curling Scholarship
audience: Alberta youth curlers eligible for U20 sanctioned season
notes: Curling Alberta's scholarships page did not return any content when checked, so nothing here is confirmed for the new cycle. Contact Curling Alberta before you plan on it.
description: $3,000 for an Alberta youth curler with strong marks who is eligible for U20 sanctioned competition during the academic year. Named after Hec Gervais, one of Alberta curling's greats.

title: Lethbridge County Bursary Program
audience: First-year post-secondary students who are residents of Lethbridge County
notes: Worth checking: Lethbridge County only advertises the Community Benefit Scholarship, so this may be the same award under an older name. Contact the County before applying to both.
description: Lethbridge County gives out three $1,500 bursaries a year to county residents entering their first year of post-secondary. Financial need is part of the selection.

title: MindFuel CDL-Rockies Opportunities Scholarship
audience: Prairie Grade 12 graduates entering a first-year undergraduate STEM program
notes: MindFuel's page publishes two different deadlines for this same award, June 30 in the eligibility panel and July 18 under Key Dates, so treat any date you see there with suspicion. The 2026 call is closed and the site says the next one opens in Spring 2027 without naming a day, which is why no deadline is shown here.
description: Two awards from MindFuel and Creative Destruction Lab Rockies for Grade 12 students graduating from an Alberta, Saskatchewan or Manitoba high school and entering a first-year undergraduate STEM program at an accredited post-secondary institution in those three provinces. Each is paid in two parts: $1,000 in first year, then $1,500 in second year if you hold an 80 per cent average. Applications from underrepresented groups in STEM are explicitly encouraged, though that is a priority rather than a requirement.
metaDetail: Paid $1,000 in first year, $1,500 in second.

title: High School Apprenticeship Scholarship
audience: Alberta high school students registered in the Registered Apprenticeship Program (RAP) or Career and Technology Studies (CTS) apprenticeship pathway
notes: There is no application and no deadline. You consent to be considered in your MyTradesecrets profile and keep your address current. Recipients are notified by November 1 each year.
description: $1,000 for finishing the requirements of the Registered Apprenticeship Program or a CTS Apprenticeship Pathway through an Alberta high school. You have to be a Canadian citizen, permanent resident or protected person, an Alberta resident by the address in MyTradesecrets, and not a previous RAP/CTS scholarship recipient. Visa students are not eligible.

title: High School Apprenticeship Scholarship: Bright Futures
audience: Alberta high school students registered in both RAP and a CTS Apprenticeship Pathway
notes: There is no application and no deadline. You consent to be considered in your MyTradesecrets profile and keep your address current. Recipients are notified by November 1 each year.
description: $2,000, the larger of the two high school apprenticeship scholarships. On top of everything the $1,000 award requires, you have to be registered as an Alberta apprentice in the Registered Apprenticeship Program with RAP credits and have completed a CTS Apprenticeship Pathway.

title: 4-H Canada Scholarships
audience: Active 4-H members in Alberta applying to post-secondary or trades programs
notes: Several streams with different amounts and sponsors: MNP ($2,000, business programs), Maizex ($4,000, crop science), Campbellbrook ($2,000, trades and apprenticeship), TD ($3,000, agriculture and agri-business) and John Deere ($1,000). You have to be a senior 4-H member. Deadline is rolled forward from last cycle.
description: 4-H Canada offers scholarships of $3,000 to active and in-good-standing 4-H members in Alberta who are pursuing post-secondary or trades education. Six different scholarship streams are available to support your continued learning. Applicants must demonstrate their commitment to 4-H and meet all membership requirements.

title: Dr. MacEwan Literary Arts Scholarship
audience: Alberta students 25 or younger demonstrating talent and clear goals in literary arts
notes: Deadline for all four Alberta Foundation for the Arts scholarship programs is March 1 every year.
description: $3,000 a year for an Alberta writer aged 25 or under, named for Grant MacEwan, author and former Lieutenant Governor of Alberta. One award is given annually, and the jury wants to see real literary ambition.

title: Alberta Foundation for the Arts Film and Video Arts Scholarship
audience: Alberta students 25 or younger demonstrating talent and goals in film and video arts
notes: Deadline for all four Alberta Foundation for the Arts scholarship programs is March 1 every year.
description: The Alberta Foundation for the Arts gives $7,000 annually to an Alberta student aged 25 or under working in film and video.

title: Alberta Foundation for the Arts Performing Arts Scholarship
audience: Alberta students 25 or younger demonstrating talent and goals in performing arts
notes: Deadline for all four Alberta Foundation for the Arts scholarship programs is March 1 every year.
description: Alberta Culture awards this $7,000 scholarship annually to recognize exceptional talent and dedication in the performing arts. It's open to Alberta students aged 25 or younger who are pursuing their passion in dance, theatre, music, and other performing disciplines. Applicants should demonstrate both artistic ability and clear goals in advancing their performing arts career.

title: Alberta Foundation for the Arts Visual Arts Scholarship
audience: Alberta students 25 or younger demonstrating talent and goals in visual arts
notes: Deadline for all four Alberta Foundation for the Arts scholarship programs is March 1 every year.
description: Alberta Culture awards this $7,000 scholarship annually to recognize exceptional talent and achievement in visual arts. Open to Alberta students aged 25 or younger who demonstrate strong artistic ability and clear goals in visual arts studies or practice. One award is given each year to a deserving student showing promise in this creative field.

title: ENMAX Scholarship
audience: Grade 12 students with a parent or guardian at ENMAX
notes: Administered by EducationMatters through one application for all CBE and Calgary Catholic awards. Applications open March 1; most close May 30, a few May 1. Confirm this award's own deadline in the portal before you rely on the date here.
description: Two awards for students whose parent or guardian is a permanent ENMAX employee or retiree. Two reference letters required.
metaDetail: A parent or guardian must work at ENMAX.

title: Alberta Blue Cross Indigenous Scholarship
audience: Indigenous (First Nations, Métis, or Inuit) Alberta residents enrolled full-time in a post-secondary program of at least 2 years
notes: Applications open October 5, 2026.
description: Alberta Blue Cross awards this $1,500 scholarship to Indigenous (First Nations, Métis, or Inuit) students who are enrolled full-time in post-secondary programs of at least 2 years in duration. Nine scholarships are awarded annually to recognize and support Indigenous learners pursuing their education. Applicants cannot have previously received this award.

title: Indspire Building Brighter Futures Bursaries and Scholarships
audience: First Nations, Inuit and Métis students in post-secondary, trades or apprenticeships
notes: One application covers every Indspire bursary, scholarship and award you qualify for. Cutoffs are August 1, November 1 and February 1 at 11:59 p.m. EST. Have your Indigenous card (front and back), your most recent grades and proof of full-time enrolment ready before you start.
description: Indspire is the largest non-governmental funder of Indigenous post-secondary students in Canada, with more than $190 million awarded since 1996. First Nations, Inuit and Métis students in college, university, skilled trades, apprenticeship and technology programs all qualify. You need to be studying full time in Canada with at least a 60 percent course load, and you can hold one Indspire award per academic year. Bursaries go on financial need, scholarships on merit. Decisions take three to six weeks and only successful applicants are contacted.

title: Grant MacEwan United World College Scholarship
audience: High school students from across Alberta demonstrating exceptional potential in intellectual curiosity, leadership, and resilience
description: Grant MacEwan United World College offers this scholarship to high school students across Alberta who demonstrate exceptional potential in intellectual curiosity, leadership, and resilience. The award supports students who show promise in these key areas as they pursue post-secondary education.

title: Lois Hole Humanities and Social Sciences Scholarship
audience: Alberta students enrolled full-time in the Faculty of Humanities, Social Sciences, or Arts at an Alberta post-secondary institution
description: This $5,000 scholarship supports Alberta students pursuing full-time studies in Humanities, Social Sciences, or Arts at an Alberta post-secondary institution. The award recognizes academic excellence and commitment to these disciplines that build critical thinking and cultural understanding.
notes: No public application deadline. Recipients are selected by the Student Awards Office at participating Alberta institutions. Contact yours to be considered.

title: Louise McKinney Post-Secondary Scholarship
audience: Alberta students with outstanding academic achievement at a post-secondary institution in Alberta
description: The Louise McKinney Post-Secondary Scholarship recognizes Alberta students who demonstrate outstanding academic achievement while enrolled at a post-secondary institution within the province. This $2,500 award supports high-performing students pursuing their studies at Alberta's colleges and universities.
notes: There is no province-wide deadline. Each post-secondary institution sets its own date and gets a limited number of awards, so ask your school's Student Awards Office as soon as you register. Selection is on academic standing.

title: Mildred Rowe Weston Memorial Scholarship
audience: Alberta students who completed at least three courses through ADLC as shown on Alberta Transcript of High School Achievement
description: $1,000 for an Alberta student who has completed at least three courses through the Alberta Distance Learning Centre.
notes: No separate application. Students are automatically considered when they apply for the Alexander Rutherford Scholarship; recipients are chosen on Grade 12 averages.

title: Tiessen Foundation Broadcast Scholarship
audience: Alberta high school graduates enrolled full-time in a post-secondary program related to broadcasting
description: The Tiessen Foundation gives $750 to an Alberta graduate entering full-time post-secondary studies in broadcasting.

title: UCalgary President's Admission Scholarship
audience: First-year University of Calgary students with a 95%+ admission average
notes: Open to students of any citizenship.
description: The University of Calgary awards this $5,000 scholarship automatically to first-year students admitted with a 95% or higher average. No separate application is required; eligible students receive the award upon admission to any faculty at the University of Calgary.

title: MacEwan University Chancellor's Scholarship
audience: Canadian citizens or permanent residents entering a MacEwan degree program from high school with an 80%+ average
notes: Admission deadline drives it: apply for admission by March 1 for fall entry or July 1 for winter. You are considered automatically, there is no separate scholarship application.
description: MacEwan University awards this competitive scholarship to Canadian citizens and permanent residents entering a MacEwan degree program from high school with strong academic performance. The award is automatically considered upon admission and ranges from $2,999 to $14,000 depending on your admission average, with the potential to be renewed each year as long as you maintain your GPA.

title: Mount Royal University Entrance Scholarship
audience: Grade 12 students entering any MRU program with an 80%+ average
notes: Heads up: Mount Royal had not posted the next cycle date when this was checked in August 2026, so this is last year's date rolled forward. Confirm on their site before you plan around it.
description: Mount Royal University awards entrance scholarships to graduating high school students with strong academic achievement. Recipients must maintain an 80%+ average and be entering any MRU program. With over $5.5 million awarded annually across all faculties, this is a major opportunity for Alberta students seeking to pursue post-secondary education at MRU.

title: ATCO Indigenous Education High School Merit Award
audience: Self-identified First Nations, Inuit, or Métis students enrolled full-time in Grades 10–12 in Canada
notes: Closes October 2 at 6:00 p.m. MST. One of the few merit awards open to students who are still in high school (Grades 10 to 12). You have to reapply each year, and children of ATCO employees are not eligible. Preference goes to students from Indigenous communities where ATCO operates.
description: ATCO's $750 merit award for self-identified First Nations, Inuit, or Métis students in Grades 10 to 12 anywhere in Canada, based on marks. You can win it in more than one year, but you have to reapply each time. Children of ATCO employees can't enter.

title: TC Energy STEM & Trades Scholarships
audience: Students entering or enrolled in a STEM or trades program who reside near TC Energy operations in Canada
notes: The 2026 window ran January 21 to May 1 and is closed. TC Energy has not posted 2027 dates yet, so these are the 2026 dates rolled forward.
description: TC Energy offers $5,000 STEM scholarships and $2,500 trades scholarships to students entering or enrolled in post-secondary STEM or trades programs who reside near TC Energy operations in Canada. Over 800 scholarships are available nationwide. Applicants must verify their community eligibility and are not eligible if they are dependants of TC Energy employees.

title: RBC Ignite Scholarship
audience: Canadians ages 16–20 taking a job-ready skills course or certification in Canada
notes: Cycle 2 runs June 23 to 1 p.m. on October 1, 2026, but RBC closes the portal early once the 500 awards are gone, so treat the date as a ceiling and apply early.
description: RBC Ignite pays $1,500 toward job-ready skills and certifications for Canadians aged 16 to 20: lifeguarding, first aid, coding, language training, graphic design, coaching certification, and more. Current high school students can apply.

title: MADD Canada Youth Bursary Fund
audience: Young Canadians severely injured or who lost an immediate family member in an impaired driving crash
notes: Deadline is May 31 every year. One $10,000 Louise Twerdy bursary plus additional $5,000 bursaries each year. You download the application form from the MADD site.
description: MADD Canada's Youth Bursary Fund supports young Canadians who have been personally affected by impaired driving, whether through serious injury or the loss of an immediate family member. This $10,000 award (top prize: Louise Joanne Twerdy Award) helps recipients pursue full-time studies at an approved post-secondary institution. Applicants must demonstrate their commitment to education while carrying the impact of an impaired driving tragedy.

title: Cenovus Energy Indigenous Scholarship
audience: Indigenous students near Cenovus operating areas, in any full-time program
notes: Part of Indspire's Building Brighter Futures. One application covers every Indspire award you qualify for, and it stays in the running for all three cutoffs: August 1, November 1 and February 1 at 11:59 p.m. EST. Apply at indspire.microsoftcrmportals.com and use one account only.
description: Cenovus pays $5,000 a year to First Nations, Métis and Inuit students living near its operating areas, renewable for up to four years within a five year period. Cenovus lists mechanical, chemical and petroleum engineering, geology, business and accounting, engineering and geoscience technology, power engineering, data science, digital technology and cybersecurity, but any full-time degree, diploma or certified trade is eligible.

title: Calgary Black Chambers Legacy Entrance Scholarship
audience: Black Canadian students graduating from a Calgary-region high school and entering first-year post-secondary
notes: Most Calgary Black Chambers scholarships close June 1 at midnight, though a few named awards use other dates. Applications usually go through the Calgary Foundation grant interface.
description: The Calgary Black Chambers Legacy Entrance Scholarship provides two awards of $2,500 each to Black Canadian students graduating from a high school in the Calgary region and entering their first year of post-secondary education. Applicants must have a minimum 70% GPA, and financial need will be considered as part of the selection process. Eligible schools include those located in Airdrie, Calgary, Chestermere, Cochrane, High River, Okotoks, Springbank, Strathmore, and Diamond Valley.

title: Skills Canada Alberta Terry Cooke Legacy Scholarship
audience: Top-scoring secondary school student representing Alberta at the Skills Canada National Competition
notes: Separate from the WorldSkills Provincial Champion Scholarship.
description: Awarded automatically to the top-scoring secondary student on Team Alberta at the Skills Canada National Competition: $5,000 a year toward post-secondary in their trade, for up to four years. There is no application.

title: Canada's Luckiest Student
audience: All students in Canada
notes: The link points at the 2026 contest page and will break when the 2027 contest launches. Search Student Life Network for the current Canada's Luckiest Student if it 404s.
description: Canada's Luckiest Student is an annual giveaway open to all students in Canada, with no essay or grades required to enter. The prize bundle includes a year of rent, $2,000 in groceries, a trip for two to the Galapagos, and a $20,000 cheque. Entries are free and take about 2 minutes to complete, with earlier submissions receiving more chances to win.
metaDetail: A free two-minute entry, no essay or grades; earlier entries get more chances.

title: Wolf Scholars Program
audience: Canadian citizens or permanent residents entering U of T Faculty of Arts & Science (St. George) with 90–100% average
notes: Open to 400+ Arts & Science programs. Applications open September 11, 2026 and close November 2, 2026.
description: A fully funded route through U of T's Faculty of Arts & Science on the St. George campus: tuition, fees, living stipend, travel, internships, mentorship, and seminars. Up to 16 scholars a year, drawn from Canadian citizens and permanent residents with a 90 to 100% average. Commerce is excluded.

targetInstitutions: University of Toronto Faculty of Arts & Science (St. George)

title: Electronic Recycling Association Scholarship
audience: Students in Canada who run an e-waste collection event in their community
description: Not an application form: you plan and run an e-waste collection drive, then submit a report on it. Winners receive cash plus refurbished technology. Open to full- and part-time students anywhere in Canada.
metaDetail: You run a collection drive and submit a report on it.

title: Alberta Masonic Higher Education Bursary
audience: Alberta and NWT residents with financial need entering post-secondary
notes: 30 bursaries of $6,000 awarded annually. Based on financial need and scholastic ability. First-year students given priority. Deadline is Feb 1 at noon.
description: The Alberta Masonic Foundation gives out 30 bursaries of $6,000 each year to first-year post-secondary students from Alberta and the NWT, weighing both marks and financial need.

title: Alberta Junior Athletic Award
audience: Alberta residents competing on a designated provincial junior sport team and entering post-secondary
notes: Your team coach nominates you, you do not apply on your own. Nominations reach Alberta Student Aid by January 15. Applications reopen in early August. You submit a transcript and an essay on your extracurriculars and goals.
description: This $800 award recognizes Alberta residents who compete on designated provincial junior sports teams (ACAC and AUAA sanctioned) and are entering post-secondary studies. To qualify, applicants must maintain a minimum 2.0 GPA and apply through Alberta Student Aid.

title: Alberta Golf Association Foundation Scholarships
audience: Alberta golfers entering post-secondary
notes: Heads up: the Alberta Golf Foundation had not posted the next cycle date when this was checked in August 2026, so this is last year's date rolled forward. Confirm on their site before you plan around it.
description: The Alberta Golf Association Foundation offers over 50 scholarships annually totalling approximately $50,000 to support Alberta golfers pursuing post-secondary education. Awards recognize strong academic performance, demonstrated financial need, volunteer contributions, and active participation in golf. This is an excellent opportunity for talented golfers to offset education costs while pursuing their goals.
metaDetail: Over 50 awards a year, on grades, need, volunteering and golf.

title: Football Alberta Scholarships
audience: Graduating Grade 12 ASAA tackle football players continuing to play at the post-secondary level in Alberta
notes: The link goes to the Football Alberta home page because the scholarship page moves each year. Look under their programs menu in the spring.
description: Eight $2,000 scholarships a year for graduating Grade 12 tackle football players continuing to play at an accredited Alberta post-secondary institution. You need to be registered full-time and on a university or junior roster.

title: ASAA Pay It Forward Scholarship
audience: Grade 12 Alberta student-athletes who coached or officiated at the school or community level
notes: Deadline is April 29 every year. Applications go to the School Sport Alberta office and then to your zone. You can include a picture or short video of your volunteer work.
description: For Grade 12 student-athletes who coach or officiate: one $500 award per ASAA zone, for students who played ASAA-sanctioned sports and gave time back to younger athletes.

title: Queen's Platinum Jubilee Scholarship for Performing Arts
audience: Alberta performing artists 25 or younger enrolled in a performing arts training program
notes: This is not the citizenship award of a similar name, and it does not need a school nomination. You apply directly through the GATE Front Office system, and first time users have to email registrationafa@gov.ab.ca at least five business days ahead to get login credentials, so do not leave that to the last week. The application wants a two page letter, a resume, a program description, proof of age, a reference letter and audition materials.
description: The Queen's Platinum Jubilee Scholarship for Performing Arts awards $7,000 to one young Alberta performing artist showing extraordinary talent and potential. The discipline rotates on a three year cycle through music, theatre and dance, and the March 1, 2027 round is the music year. You have to be 25 or younger at the deadline, have lived in Alberta for a full year, and be enrolled in an eligible training program: an undergraduate degree with a performing arts focus, a technical or conservatory school, or a recognized mentorship or master class. Graduate programs do not count.

title: Alberta Centennial Award
audience: Alberta high school graduates nominated for the Premier's Citizenship Award who are enrolling in post-secondary
notes: You have to be nominated for the Premier's Citizenship Award by your school first. The 2027 intake opens March 1, 2027 through the GATE Front Office system.
description: An oddly specific $2,005 (the award marks Alberta's 2005 centennial) for graduates nominated for the Premier's Citizenship Award who are enrolling in post-secondary. Nomination comes through your school, so start with your administration.

title: Aufricht Family Fund Student Award
audience: Graduating Calgary CBE or CCSD students entering UCalgary or SAIT with financial need
notes: The provider had not posted a date for the new cycle when this was checked in August 2026, so this is last cycle's deadline rolled forward. Confirm before you plan around it.
description: The Aufricht Family Fund provides $4,000–$5,000 awards to graduating Calgary high school students entering post-secondary studies with demonstrated financial need. This renewable award supports students for up to 3 years if they maintain a 2.0+ cumulative GPA and remain enrolled full-time. Applicants from Calgary CBE or CCSD schools who plan to attend UCalgary or SAIT are encouraged to apply, provided they do not already hold an equal or greater award from EducationMatters or the Calgary Foundation.

title: Elmer and Ona Hansen Memorial Fund
audience: Alberta rural farm youth entering first-year post-secondary with no prior post-secondary enrollment
notes: Multiple large awards: 1 × $20,000, 1 × $15,000, 1 × $10,000, 7 × $5,000. Applicants must be Alberta rural farm young persons who have not previously started or completed any post-secondary program. Applications open in May.
description: Between $5,000 and $20,000 for rural Alberta farm youth entering their first year of post-secondary. You must come from a farm and have no prior post-secondary education. Among the largest awards available to rural students in the province.

title: AAAF Memorial Bursary
audience: Alberta residents entering an agriculture or environmental science program at a college or university
description: The Association of Alberta Agricultural Fieldmen offers this $1,000 bursary to Alberta residents entering agriculture or environmental science programs at post-secondary institutions. Applicants must submit high school marks and a letter of acceptance from their chosen college or university. Apply through your local County agricultural office.

title: AHSRA Scholarships
audience: Grade 12 Alberta students; AHSRA members and volunteers are weighted, but non-participants may apply
notes: Submit by mail to the AHSRA Scholarship Coordinator.
description: The Alberta High School Rodeo Association (AHSRA) offers multiple scholarships for Grade 12 students who are active members or volunteers in the association. The list includes Merit Awards, NHSRA Merit Awards, Canadian Finals Scholarships, the Presidents Award, the Teskey Top Hand Award, and the Raffle Scholarship, covering both athletic achievement and community involvement. A single application covers all available AHSRA scholarships.

title: Roane Family Bursary for Queen's University
audience: Students from Canmore, Banff, or Morley attending Queen's University
notes: Administered through Bow Valley High School, whose scholarship page still lists a 2023 deadline. Ask the school directly before you plan on it.
description: The Roane Family Bursary supports students from Canmore, Banff, or Morley who are attending Queen's University. This $5,000 annual bursary is awarded based on demonstrated financial need. Applicants should contact their school guidance counsellor for application details.

title: Volleyball Alberta Hugh Hoyles Scholarship Fund
audience: Alberta residents selected to a Team Alberta volleyball program
notes: The link goes to the Volleyball Alberta home page. Look under their programs or awards menu in the spring.
description: Volleyball Alberta offers the Hugh Hoyles Scholarship Fund to support student-athletes excelling in volleyball. This $500 award recognizes Alberta residents who have been selected to a Team Alberta volleyball program. Applicants may submit only one application per calendar year.

title: PEO Florence E. Taylor Charitable Scholarship Fund
audience: Female Alberta students in their first or second year at an Alberta or Saskatchewan post-secondary institution
description: The P.E.O. Sisterhood funds female students from Alberta in their first or second year at an Alberta or Saskatchewan institution, with financial need part of the selection. There is no central application; contact your nearest Alberta P.E.O. chapter.

title: University of Alberta Turtle Spirit Pathway Award
audience: Domestic students applying to a UAlberta direct-entry undergraduate program with no prior post-secondary and demonstrated financial barriers
notes: The 2027 intake runs October 1, 2026 to February 15, 2027, with offers from mid-April.
description: The University of Alberta offers the Turtle Spirit Pathway Award to First Nations, Métis and Inuit students who are entering a UAlberta direct-entry undergraduate program with no prior post-secondary coursework and who have demonstrated financial challenges and barriers to attending university. Students are considered for up to $8,000 per year, up to 20 new students qualify each year, and applicants must complete a separate application through the Awards Hub after submitting their UAlberta admission application.

title: Beyond the North Scholarship
audience: Grade 12 students graduating from a Fairview area high school in northern Alberta and entering first-year post-secondary
notes: Calgary Foundation lists this one with a June 1 deadline. You apply through the Calgary Foundation awards portal.
description: Started in 2021 by Fairview area alumni and run through the Calgary Foundation, this award funds Grade 12 graduates from Fairview area high schools in northern Alberta entering first-year studies at any Canadian post-secondary institution.

title: Charmaine Letourneau Scholarship
audience: Alberta residents who are deaf or hard of hearing entering a post-secondary or vocational program
description: The Edmonton Community Foundation awards the Charmaine Letourneau Scholarship to Alberta residents who are deaf or hard of hearing as they enter a post-secondary or vocational program. Applicants must demonstrate financial need and knowledge of sign language, with school and community leadership also considered in selection.

title: Royal Canadian Legion Ladies Auxiliary AB-NWT Bursary
audience: Alberta and NWT students entering first-term post-secondary with a family connection to veterans, RCMP, firefighters, or Legion members
notes: Each Legion branch sets its own deadline, eligibility details and application process, so contact your local branch rather than working to a fixed date. Must be a graduate of the current or previous year and under 21. Eligible family connections include children and grandchildren of veterans, current Canadian Forces, RCMP and reserve personnel.
description: The Royal Canadian Legion Ladies Auxiliary in Alberta and the Northwest Territories offers this $500 bursary to graduating high school students entering their first year of post-secondary education. To qualify, applicants must have a family connection to veterans, current Canadian Forces members, RCMP officers, reserve personnel, firefighters (paid or volunteer), or Legion Auxiliary or Branch members. Recipients must be under 21 years old and can contact their nearest Alberta Legion branch to apply.

title: UFCW Canada Begg's-Dowling-Mathieu Scholarship
audience: UFCW Canada members or their dependents/spouses entering full-time post-secondary studies in Canada
notes: 18 scholarships of $1,000 allocated nationally by region. Apply online at ufcw.ca.
description: UFCW Canada offers this $1,000 scholarship to members in good standing or their dependents and spouses who are entering full-time post-secondary studies in Canada. The scholarship recognizes enrollment and passion for learning rather than top grades. Applicants must have a parent or guardian who is an active UFCW Canada member to be eligible.

title: UFCW Local 401 Scholarships
audience: UFCW Local 401 (Alberta) members or their dependents entering post-secondary

Applicants must demonstrate scientific curiosity, extracurricular involvement, and community contributions. Two letters of recommendation are required. The recipient also receives an invitation to visit the Perimeter Institute for Theoretical Physics.

Canadian residents (excluding Quebec) who are currently enrolled in high school are eligible. Parental or guardian consent is required for applicants under 18.

The top prize is $2,000; a runner-up award of $500 is also given. Quebec residents and those attending post-secondary during the 2025-2026 school year are not eligible.

title: Communication Contest for the Deaf and Hard of Hearing

The contest is organized at the local district level through Optimist Club chapters across Canada, the US, and the Caribbean, with up to 45 awards available.

description: Cypress County Council awards two $1,000 scholarships a year to high school students from the County who are heading to post-secondary, with preference given to those entering a technical program.
