Two rules decide most of it: the piece has to be memorized, and you need the top mark in your class or at least 85 per cent. The 2026 festival ran March 16 to 26; registration for the next one opens through MusicFestivalSuite and the site had not posted its dates when this was checked.
description: The Airdrie Rotary festival attaches scholarships to its music and speech classes, awarded to competitors who take the highest mark in their class or earn at least 85 per cent. You have to live or study music in Rocky View County to be eligible, and students away at post-secondary can still qualify through a parent living in the county.
metaDetail: Many small awards, decided by your festival mark.

title: Jack Paterson Memorial Scholarship
audience: Alberta students aged 17 to 25 who volunteer in the Bow Valley Credit Union service area
notes: The volunteering has to be in one of the credit union's own communities: Acheson, Airdrie, Banff, Calgary, Canmore or Cochrane, and within the last two years. You do not have to bank there. Applications run June 17 to August 31, results by September 16 and money by September 30, which makes this one of the few awards that pays in time for the fall term.
description: A single $4,000 award from Bow Valley Credit Union for an Alberta student between 17 and 25 who is enrolled or accepted full time at a Canadian post-secondary institution and has volunteered in the credit union's service area in the past two years. You submit proof of enrolment, proof of Alberta residency, a resume, and a statement or video about your goals.
metaDetail: Volunteering in the credit union's own towns is the filter.

title: Bow Valley Credit Union Scholarship
audience: Alberta students aged 17 to 25 entering or continuing full-time post-secondary study
notes: Two awards, and no membership requirement: the credit union asks for Alberta residency, not an account. The same June 17 to August 31 window as the Jack Paterson award, and one application covers what you qualify for. Trades and technical programs count.
description: Two $2,000 scholarships from Bow Valley Credit Union for Alberta residents between 17 and 25 who are enrolled or accepted at an accredited Canadian post-secondary institution in a full-time undergraduate or technical program. The application asks for proof of enrolment, proof of Alberta residency, a resume, and a short statement or video about your educational goals.
metaDetail: No membership needed, and trades programs count.

title: Anne Beaty Memorial Scholarship
audience: Alberta high school students and graduates headed into writing, journalism or communications
notes: Run by the Airdrie magazine airdrielife, in memory of a writer who worked there and at the Airdrie Public Library. The selection committee includes her two daughters and the magazine's publisher, which tells you the application is read by people looking for a voice rather than a transcript. The magazine does not publish an amount or a fixed closing date, so watch its site in the spring.
description: An annual award from airdrielife magazine for an Alberta high school student or graduate who is serious about the written word, going to one applicant a year on academic record, community involvement and leadership. It was created in 2017 in memory of Anne Beaty, who wrote for the magazine from 2010 to 2016.
metaDetail: One recipient a year, chosen for the writing.

title: Calgary Black Chambers Business Scholarship
audience: Black students in a Commerce or Business Administration program, entering second year or beyond
notes: One application is considered for all four awards, so there is nothing to gain from picking one. The geography is wider than the name suggests: a graduate of an Airdrie, Chestermere, Cochrane, Diamond Valley, High River, Okotoks, Springbank or Strathmore high school qualifies at any Canadian institution, and everyone else has to be at a Calgary one. The provider had not posted the new cycle when this was checked in August 2026, so this is last cycle's deadline rolled forward.
description: Four awards for Black Canadian citizens or permanent residents in a full-time Commerce or Business Administration degree or diploma, entering second year or beyond: the ATB Community Leadership Scholarship and the KPMG Academic Excellence Scholarship at $5,000, and the Academic Excellence at MRU and TD Business Leadership scholarships at $7,000. It needs a GPA of at least 2.7 or 70 per cent and one reference letter from a business or community leader.
metaDetail: One application, four awards, second year and beyond.

title: Calgary Black Chambers Legacy Scholarship
audience: Black students entering second year or beyond of a first undergraduate degree or diploma
notes: Eight awards makes this one of the better odds in the Calgary Foundation's list, and it is the continuing-student twin of the Legacy Entrance Scholarship rather than a competitor to it. Graduates of an Airdrie, Chestermere, Cochrane, Diamond Valley, High River, Okotoks, Springbank or Strathmore high school qualify wherever in Canada they are studying. The provider had not posted the new cycle when this was checked in August 2026, so this is last cycle's deadline rolled forward.
description: Eight awards of $2,500 each for Black Canadian citizens or permanent residents entering second year or beyond of a first undergraduate degree or diploma in full-time study. It asks for a GPA of at least 2.7 or 70 per cent, demonstrated financial need, school or community involvement, and one reference letter.
metaDetail: Eight awards, for students already at post-secondary.

title: Northwestern Alberta Foundation Student Awards
audience: Students from northwestern Alberta entering or continuing post-secondary study
notes: This is the single most useful application in the Peace Country and almost nobody outside Grande Prairie has heard of it. The foundation holds more than forty separate award funds, and one universal form puts you in front of every fund you qualify for, so the work of applying once is spread across dozens of chances. In 2025 it paid out over $60,000 across 100 awards. The window ran from April 16 to August 9 in 2026, so this is that deadline rolled forward a year and the foundation had not posted the new dates when this was checked.
description: One application to the Northwestern Alberta Foundation is considered for over forty student award funds covering sports, nursing, environmental studies, emergency services, trades, agriculture, fine arts, animal health, education, business, technology, music, tourism and hospitality. Recipients come from Grande Prairie, Peace River, High Level and other communities across the region, and awards follow students to institutions inside and outside Alberta. Decisions are sent in mid-September.
metaDetail: One form, over forty separate award funds.

title: Ron Pfau Memorial Scholarship
audience: County of Grande Prairie residents studying business, commerce or public office administration
notes: Named for a longtime County administrator, and the residency test is the County of Grande Prairie rather than the City, so a student inside city limits does not qualify on their own address. Your parents' County residence counts if you have moved away for school. County council handed administration to the Northwestern Alberta Foundation in 2024, so it now runs on the foundation's universal application and its August deadline, shown here rolled forward.
description: A $1,000 scholarship for current or former residents of the County of Grande Prairie who are Canadian citizens or landed immigrants and are entering or enrolled at an Alberta post-secondary institution in business, commerce or public office administration. Applications go through the Northwestern Alberta Foundation portal.
metaDetail: County address required, not a city one.

title: Grande Prairie Auto Group Student Award
audience: Grande Prairie city or county residents in an Automotive Service Technician program
notes: A single award, but the eligible pool is tiny: you have to live in the City or County of Grande Prairie and be registered specifically as an automotive service technician. If that is you, this is close to the best odds on the site. Five dealership general managers put it together in 2022. It is paid through the Northwestern Alberta Foundation universal application, so the deadline shown is the foundation's, rolled forward a year.
description: One award of $1,500 for a resident of the City of Grande Prairie or the County of Grande Prairie who is registered in an Automotive Service Technician program. Applications are made through the Northwestern Alberta Foundation.
metaDetail: One award, and a very small eligible pool.

title: Chief Ronald W. Clarke Fund Student Award
audience: County of Grande Prairie residents in an emergency services program
notes: The Wembley Fire Department started this in 2012 for a volunteer firefighter with 46 years of service, and the eligible programs are broader than the name suggests: nursing and physician studies count alongside firefighting and paramedicine. The fund is an endowment, so the amount depends on what it earned that year and the foundation does not publish a fixed figure. Applications run through the foundation's universal form and its August deadline, shown here rolled forward.
description: A student award for a resident of the County of Grande Prairie registered in an emergency services program, including firefighting, emergency medical services, paramedic training, nursing, physician services and enforcement services. Applicants are asked to show commitment or roots in the Peace Country. Applications are made through the Northwestern Alberta Foundation.
metaDetail: Nursing counts, not just firefighting.

title: Royal Canadian Legion Branch 54 Bursary
audience: Grande Prairie graduates with veteran ancestry
notes: Four bursaries, and the ancestry test is wider than most students assume: a grandparent or great-grandparent who served is usually enough, and the branch will tell you if you are unsure. Any program of study qualifies, which is rarer than it sounds among Legion awards. This is last cycle's August deadline rolled forward a year, since the branch had not posted the new one when this was checked.
description: Four bursaries of $750 for students who have completed Grade 12, are residents of the City or County of Grande Prairie graduating from a local high school, and are descended from a veteran. The award is open to any program of post-secondary study.
metaDetail: Four awards, and any program qualifies.

title: Grande Prairie and District Oldtimers' Association Scholarship
audience: Descendants of Grande Prairie district pioneers
notes: The eligibility line here is genuinely unusual and it is worth asking your family about before you rule yourself out: you have to be descended from a Grande Prairie district pioneer family. Many students in the Peace Country qualify and never check. The academic bar is a 70 per cent average, which is low by scholarship standards, and the association does not publish a fixed amount.
description: A scholarship for post-secondary students who are descendants of Grande Prairie district pioneers and who have maintained a minimum 70 per cent average. The value is set by the association each year.
metaDetail: For pioneer descendants, at a 70 per cent bar.

title: Perky McCullough International Excellence Scholarship
audience: Grande Prairie athletes competing at the international level
notes: The bar is real: this is for athletes with a credible path to international competition, and you need confirmation of membership in a national sport association to apply. Two awards a year. One catch that disqualifies people every cycle is that an application submitted after the event has already happened is not eligible, so apply ahead of the competition you are funding.
description: Two scholarships of $2,500 a year from the City of Grande Prairie for athletes who are or have been part of the Grande Prairie Sport Development System and show the best potential for international success. The application asks for letters of support from a coach or mentor, confirmation of national sport association membership, a goal statement covering short and long term objectives, and disclosure of other funding and sponsorships.
metaDetail: Two awards, and you must apply before the event.

title: Bob Neufeld Scholarship
audience: Grande Prairie athletes, volunteer coaches and sport officials
notes: Four awards, and this is one of the few sport scholarships anywhere that treats volunteer coaches and officials as equals with athletes, so a Grade 12 student who referees or coaches a younger division can apply on that alone. Clubs are limited to one applicant per deadline, so ask early rather than assuming your club has a spot. As with the other City award, you have to apply before the event happens.
description: Up to four scholarships of $1,200 a year from the City of Grande Prairie for individuals pursuing excellence in their sport. Individual athletes, volunteer coaches and sport officials may all apply, and the application asks for a goal statement with performance history, letters of support from a coach or mentor, and confirmation of national sport association membership.
metaDetail: Coaches and referees apply on equal footing.

title: Rotary Club of Grande Prairie Scholarship
audience: Grade 12 students at Grande Prairie high schools
notes: One of the awards is set aside for a student heading to trade school rather than university, which is worth knowing because trades applicants often skip Rotary awards assuming they are a poor fit. The application is built around a personal statement on Rotary's core values of service, integrity, leadership and diversity, so write to those four words directly. This is last cycle's May deadline rolled forward a year.
description: A $2,000 scholarship from the Rotary Club of Grande Prairie for Grade 12 students at local high schools who are completing diploma requirements and are registered for full-time post-secondary study starting the fall after graduation. One award is available for a student entering a trade school program of at least six months. The application requires a personal statement on Rotary's core values and two letters of reference.
metaDetail: One award is reserved for trade school.

title: Weyerhaeuser Grande Prairie Local Scholarship
audience: Grande Prairie Public School Division graduates
notes: Two awards, restricted to graduates of the public division, so Catholic and Peace Wapiti students are out. Certain programs get preference and the application form is where that list lives, so read it before you write anything. Awards are presented at the division's Striving for Excellence dinner in October, months after you graduate. This is last cycle's deadline rolled forward.
description: Two scholarships of $500 each from Weyerhaeuser for Grande Prairie Public School Division graduates. Preference is given to students entering specific programs identified on the application form.
metaDetail: Public division graduates only.

title: GPPSD Career and Technology Studies Scholarship
audience: Grande Prairie Public School Division students in CTS courses
notes: The Education Foundation funds two of these at each of the division's two high schools, so four are given out and the pool is only students taking CTS courses at those schools. That is unusually good odds for a $1,000 award. The division's page was still showing an old cycle's dates when this was checked, so confirm the current deadline with your counsellor rather than trusting the posted one.
description: Scholarships of $1,000 for Grande Prairie Public School Division students studying welding, construction, fashion design, automotive technology, design studies, cosmetology, foods, electronics, communications or business education. Awards are presented at the division's Striving for Excellence Awards Dinner.
metaDetail: Two per school, for CTS students.

title: Striving for Nursing Excellence Bursary
audience: Students in nursing programs in the Grande Prairie region
notes: The range is wide because the committee sizes the award to the applicant, so a strong file is worth applying with even if you only need part of it. Every nursing credential is eligible, from licensed practical nursing through to a doctorate, which makes this unusually open compared to most nursing awards. Applications go by email to the hospital foundation. This is last cycle's May deadline rolled forward a year.
description: A bursary of between $500 and $5,000 from the Grande Prairie Regional Hospital Foundation for students in licensed practical nursing, nursing, psychiatric nursing, nurse practitioner, master of nursing or nursing doctorate programs. The committee looks for commitment, dedication and growth potential. The application asks for a cover letter, resume, two letters of reference, a course outline and transcripts.
metaDetail: Every nursing credential qualifies, LPN through doctorate.

title: Sarah Joan Alward Bursary
audience: Health care students who will work in northwestern Alberta
notes: The catch is the return of service agreement: taking this money commits you to a year of work in northwestern Alberta after you finish. If you were planning to come home anyway that is free money, and if you were not, read the agreement before you sign. You also need at least one year of study already completed, so this is not an award to apply for in Grade 12.
description: A bursary of between $1,000 and $2,500 from the Grande Prairie Regional Hospital Foundation for students in a health care field who have completed at least one year at an accredited institution, are filling an identified occupational need in northwestern Alberta, and will sign a one year return of service agreement.
metaDetail: Comes with a one year return of service.

title: Northern Alberta Rural Physicians Fund
audience: Medical students who attended high school in northern Alberta
notes: The eligibility line is drawn on a map: you had to attend high school in an Alberta community at or north of the 54th parallel, which takes in Grande Prairie, Peace River, High Level, Fort McMurray and Grande Cache. Worth flagging in Grade 12 even though you cannot apply yet, because it is a reason to keep your northern high school records handy years later.
description: One or more awards totalling up to $10,000 a year from the Grande Prairie Regional Hospital Foundation for medical students accepted at or enrolled in a Canadian medical school who intend to practise in rural northern Alberta at or north of the 54th parallel. Applicants must have attended high school in an Alberta community at or north of that line, and sign a return of service agreement on completion.
metaDetail: Drawn on a map: high school north of the 54th.

title: Queen Elizabeth II Platinum Jubilee Citizenship Award
audience: Graduating Alberta Grade 12 students who hold a Premier's Citizenship Award nomination
notes: Your school nominates one graduating student for the Premier's Citizenship Award, and that nomination is what makes you eligible here, so the deadline that actually matters is your school's internal one. The 2027 intake opens March 1, 2027 and closes June 1, 2027 through the GATE Front Office system. The Alberta Centennial Award runs off the same nomination.
description: Eight young Albertans a year receive a $7,000 scholarship and a medallion for citizenship, leadership and community service, not for grades. You have to hold your school's Premier's Citizenship Award nomination first, be a Canadian citizen, permanent resident or protected person, be an Alberta resident, and be enrolled full time in a post-secondary program for the fall or winter term. The application wants a Record of Accomplishments chart covering your community work and two reference letters of no more than two pages each.

title: Optimist International Essay Contest
audience: Students under 19 who have not yet finished secondary school
notes: April 15 is the date your District has to send its winner to Optimist International, and the Districts send to that date every year. Your own deadline is set by your sponsoring club and is much earlier: club contests run in early February, and clubs pass their winner up by the end of that month. Contact a local club in the fall rather than waiting for a posted date. Alberta clubs sit in Zones 3, 5 and 6 of the AMSNW District.
description: Optimist International runs an annual essay contest with a set topic, and club winners advance to a District competition worth a $2,500 scholarship. You have to be under 19 as of October 1 of the contest year and not yet finished secondary school. Entries go through a local Optimist Club, and you have to enter in the District where you live, which for Alberta students is the Alberta, Montana, Saskatchewan and Northern Wyoming District.

title: Optimist International Oratorical Contest
audience: Students under 19 who have not yet finished secondary school
notes: No date is shown here because there is no single one to show. Club contests are usually held by late March but each sponsoring club sets its own, the Alberta Zone contest runs in April, and the District contest sits inside the third quarter District meeting in May. The date you need is your local club's, so contact one in the fall. Alberta clubs sit in Zones 3, 5 and 6 of the AMSNW District.
description: Optimist International runs an annual speech contest on a set topic, judged live rather than on paper. You have to be under 19 as of October 1 of the contest year and not yet finished secondary school. You start at a local Optimist Club and win your way up through the Zone to the District, where the placings are worth $2,500, $1,500 and $1,000. This is a sibling of the Communication Contest for the Deaf and Hard of Hearing, which runs the same topic on a separate track.

title: Brooks & District Health Foundation Scholarship Fund
audience: Brooks, Duchess and Rosemary graduates entering a healthcare profession
notes: The handbook publishes no closing date for this award. It is open past Brooks Composite itself, so if you graduate from another high school in the area, ask your own office how it collects the application; the BCHS handbook is where the criteria are written down.
description: The Brooks & District Health Foundation puts one $1,000 award behind a graduate heading into a healthcare profession. You have to have attended high school in the area the Foundation serves, which it defines as Brooks, Duchess and Rosemary, and you have to be entering post-secondary education in a chosen healthcare field. The field requirement is doing the narrowing here: it is a single award, but the pool it draws from is three towns' worth of students committed to health care, not everyone graduating.
metaDetail: One award, applied for through your school.

title: Grasslands ATA Scholarship
audience: Graduating Grasslands students who are children of division teachers
notes: The handbook publishes no closing date for this award. Applications go through your Grasslands school rather than to the sponsor, and the form is a Google Doc only Grasslands students can open, so ask your school office in the fall for the date it is collecting by.
description: The Grasslands local of the Alberta Teachers' Association funds four scholarships of $1,000 each. They are for graduating Grasslands School Division students entering an accredited post-secondary program, and the qualifying condition is family: you must be the child of a past or present teacher of the division, counting anyone who taught there within the past five years. Four awards against a pool that small is unusually good odds, and the five-year window means a parent who has since left teaching still counts.
metaDetail: Four awards a year.

title: Robert Trimmer Sr. Prize in Science
audience: Grasslands Public Schools graduates in science
notes: The handbook publishes no closing date for this award. Applications go through your Grasslands school rather than to the sponsor, and the form is a Google Doc only Grasslands students can open, so ask your school office in the fall for the date it is collecting by.
description: A science prize endowed by two Grasslands graduates, Dr. Kenton Rommens and Dr. Ashley Rommens, in memory of their grandfather Robert "Bud" Trimmer Sr. It is open to graduates of Grasslands Public Schools. The handbook does not print an amount or a set of scored criteria for it, which is normal for a family-funded prize of this kind; the selection sits with the school and the donors.
metaDetail: Endowed by two Grasslands graduates, both doctors.

title: Brooks Rotary Club Award
audience: Any County of Newell high school graduate with a service record
notes: The handbook publishes no closing date for this award. It is open past Brooks Composite itself, so if you graduate from another high school in the area, ask your own office how it collects the application; the BCHS handbook is where the criteria are written down.
description: The Brooks Rotary Club gives this one on exemplary service to the community and/or the school. It goes annually to a graduate of any high school in the County of Newell who is planning to attend a post-secondary institution, so it reaches past Brooks Composite to the county's other schools. Service is the whole criterion here, not marks, which makes it one of the better fits for a student whose transcript is ordinary and whose volunteer record is not.
metaDetail: Judged on service, not marks.

title: Brooks & District Retired Teachers' Scholarship
audience: Grasslands Regional Division graduates entering post-secondary
notes: Applications go to the BCHS main office by May 15 rather than to the sponsor. One thing to read carefully: the handbook blurb says the student should already have achieved another system-wide award, but the application form itself sets no such condition, so apply and let the committee decide. The form also asks for a social insurance number.
description: Funded by the district's retired teachers for a graduating student from a Grasslands Regional Division high school, meaning Bassano, Brooks, Duchess, Rosemary or Sunrise, who is registered at a post-secondary institution and can attach proof of acceptance. Selection weighs community service and extracurricular involvement, diverse interests and talents, three letters of reference and academic achievement.
metaDetail: Three reference letters and a transcript are required.

title: LifeTouch Humanities Award
audience: The BCHS graduate with the highest combined Social Studies and English mark
notes: No application decides this one. The school works it out from the blended diploma marks in Social Studies and English, so there is nothing to submit and no date to meet.
description: A straight marks award with nothing to write. It goes to the student with the highest average across Social Studies and English combined, and the marks used are the blended marks from the diploma exam courses, so it is settled by your transcript rather than by an application committee. There is one of these and it is decided arithmetically, which means the only way to influence it is in the two courses themselves.

title: 1989 Alberta Summer Games Athletics Scholarship
audience: BCHS graduates entering kinesiology, PE, or recreation studies
notes: The handbook publishes no closing date for this award. Applications are collected by Brooks Composite High School rather than by the sponsor, and the form itself is a Google Doc only Grasslands students can open, so the date you need is the one the school sets. Ask the BCHS office in the fall.
description: One of two awards left over from the 1989 Alberta Summer Games hosted in Brooks, this one on the athletics side. It is made available annually to a Brooks Composite High School graduate planning to attend a post-secondary institution to study kinesiology, education in physical education, or any field relating to recreation, which the handbook opens out to recreation management, administration and therapy. The field of study is the requirement, not an athletic record.
metaDetail: Judged on field of study, not on sport.

title: 1989 Alberta Summer Games Fine Arts Scholarship
audience: BCHS graduates entering fine or performing arts
notes: The handbook publishes no closing date for this award. Applications are collected by Brooks Composite High School rather than by the sponsor, and the form itself is a Google Doc only Grasslands students can open, so the date you need is the one the school sets. Ask the BCHS office in the fall.
description: The fine arts half of the money the 1989 Alberta Summer Games left in Brooks. It is made available annually to a Brooks Composite High School graduate planning to attend a post-secondary institution in the fine or performing arts. Like its athletics twin it turns on what you are going to study rather than on a portfolio or an audition, so acceptance into an arts program is the thing that qualifies you.
metaDetail: No audition or portfolio required.

title: Spirit of BCHS Citizenship Award
audience: BCHS graduates recognised for citizenship and helping others
notes: The handbook publishes no closing date for this award. Applications are collected by Brooks Composite High School rather than by the sponsor, and the form itself is a Google Doc only Grasslands students can open, so the date you need is the one the school sets. Ask the BCHS office in the fall.
description: Presented annually to a Brooks Composite High School graduate going on to post-secondary, and written entirely around character rather than achievement. The handbook asks for commendable citizenship in the school and/or the community, a willingness to assist others in need, thoughtfulness and consideration toward others, and a charitable and sharing disposition. Nothing there is a metric, so this is decided by the staff who have watched you for three years.
metaDetail: Decided on character by school staff.

title: Brooks Kinsmen Citizenship Award
audience: Students with a 75% average and a strong citizenship record
notes: The handbook publishes no closing date for this award. Applications are collected by Brooks Composite High School rather than by the sponsor, and the form itself is a Google Doc only Grasslands students can open, so the date you need is the one the school sets. Ask the BCHS office in the fall.
description: The Brooks Kinsmen weigh two things together. The first is academic: an average for the year of at least 75%. The second is citizenship, which they break out into leadership involvement, the extent of that involvement, the quality of the work, and attitude toward school and fellow students. The award goes to whoever best demonstrates the combination, so a very strong record on one side does not carry it alone.
metaDetail: Needs a 75% average plus a leadership record.

title: Brooks Elks Lodge Leadership Scholarship
audience: Grade 12 students who lead by example inside the school
notes: The handbook publishes no closing date for this award. Applications are collected by Brooks Composite High School rather than by the sponsor, and the form itself is a Google Doc only Grasslands students can open, so the date you need is the one the school sets. Ask the BCHS office in the fall.
description: The Brooks Elks Lodge is looking for a Grade 12 student who sets an example others follow: a positive attitude in leadership situations, motivation to get the school population to take responsibility for its own surroundings, and dedication to the school in curricular as well as extracurricular areas. It also asks that you plan to use the money to develop those leadership skills further, so the application is partly about what comes next.
metaDetail: Asks how you will use it to lead further.

title: Brooks Masonic Foundation Scholarship
audience: The BCHS student with the best mix of marks and citizenship
notes: The handbook publishes no closing date for this award. Applications are collected by Brooks Composite High School rather than by the sponsor, and the form itself is a Google Doc only Grasslands students can open, so the date you need is the one the school sets. Ask the BCHS office in the fall.
description: The Brooks Masonic Foundation award is written in a single line: it goes to the student who exemplifies the best combination of academic ability and citizenship quality. There is no stated minimum average and no scored rubric, which means the two halves are weighed against each other rather than checked off. This is separate from the province-wide Alberta Masonic Higher Education Bursary, which is a needs-based fund with its own application.
metaDetail: Marks and citizenship weighed together.

title: Dr. Santokh Singh First Generation Canadian Scholarship
audience: First generation Canadian students in the Brooks area
notes: The handbook publishes no closing date for this award. Applications are collected by Brooks Composite High School rather than by the sponsor, and the form itself is a Google Doc only Grasslands students can open, so the date you need is the one the school sets. Ask the BCHS office in the fall.
description: The Singh family funds a $500 scholarship for a first generation Canadian student planning to pursue post-secondary education. Dr. Singh and his family choose the recipient themselves, on the basis of financial need and academic ability together. Brooks has one of the most diverse student populations in southern Alberta and very little money written for it specifically, which makes this a small award with an unusually well-matched pool.
metaDetail: Chosen by the Singh family on need and marks.

title: Marilyn Jackson Fine Arts Scholarship
audience: Students entering a fine arts program such as dance or music
notes: The handbook publishes no closing date for this award. Applications are collected by Brooks Composite High School rather than by the sponsor, and the form itself is a Google Doc only Grasslands students can open, so the date you need is the one the school sets. Ask the BCHS office in the fall.
description: Sponsored by the Newell Concert Association and awarded to a student going into a fine arts program, with dance and music named as examples rather than as the limit. The association exists to bring performance into the Brooks area, and this is the part of its work that follows a local student out of it. Acceptance into the program is what qualifies you; the handbook sets no audition or portfolio requirement.
metaDetail: Sponsored by the Newell Concert Association.

title: Knights of Columbus Scholarship
audience: Students active in their faith community with a 70% average
notes: The handbook publishes no closing date for this award. Applications are collected by Brooks Composite High School rather than by the sponsor, and the form itself is a Google Doc only Grasslands students can open, so the date you need is the one the school sets. Ask the BCHS office in the fall.
description: This one asks for a student who is actively involved in their faith community and/or actively pursuing religious studies at the post-secondary level. Beyond that it wants an active member of both the school and the community, enrolment at a post-secondary school, and above average scholastic performance, which the handbook puts at 70% or better. The 70% floor is low enough that the faith and service record is what decides it.
metaDetail: Needs faith community involvement and 70%.

title: Ron & Doreen Brandt Faculty of Education Scholarship
audience: BCHS graduates entering a teaching degree with a 75% average
notes: The handbook publishes no closing date for this award. Applications are collected by Brooks Composite High School rather than by the sponsor, and the form itself is a Google Doc only Grasslands students can open, so the date you need is the one the school sets. Ask the BCHS office in the fall.
description: Awarded annually to a Brooks Composite High School graduate who is going on to a post-secondary institution to become a teacher. To qualify you need a minimum average of 75% in your Grade 12 courses. Awards restricted to future teachers are rare outside the university faculties themselves, and this one is restricted to a single high school on top of that, so the field it competes against is very small.
metaDetail: Needs a 75% Grade 12 average.

title: Gazdarica Memorial Scholarship
audience: BCHS graduates who live in Tilley and attended Tilley School
notes: The handbook publishes no closing date for this award. Applications are collected by Brooks Composite High School rather than by the sponsor, and the form itself is a Google Doc only Grasslands students can open, so the date you need is the one the school sets. Ask the BCHS office in the fall.
description: The narrowest award in the Brooks handbook. It is made annually to a graduate of Brooks Composite High School who lives in Tilley and attended Tilley School for Grade 9, and who is planning to attend a post-secondary institution in the fall. Two conditions, both about one hamlet of a few hundred people. If you fit it, the number of students you are competing with in a given year is likely in the single digits.
metaDetail: The narrowest award in the Brooks handbook.

title: Craig Lester Agricultural & Travel Bursary
audience: Students heading into agriculture or agri-food
notes: The handbook publishes no closing date for this award. Applications are collected by Brooks Composite High School rather than by the sponsor, and the form itself is a Google Doc only Grasslands students can open, so the date you need is the one the school sets. Ask the BCHS office in the fall.
description: Craig Lester graduated from BCHS in 2000 and became an agricultural broadcast journalist; he was raised on a farm near Rolling Hills and still helps with the family operation. He created this as a scholarship and travel bursary in the spirit of bridging the gap between farmers and consumers, and it goes on an application describing your interests and your plans in agriculture and food production. The travel half is the unusual part: it is written to fund going and seeing, not only tuition.
metaDetail: Funds travel as well as tuition.

title: BCHS Construction Scholarship
audience: BCHS students who completed Construction 10, 20 and 30
notes: The handbook publishes no closing date for this award. Applications are collected by Brooks Composite High School rather than by the sponsor, and the form itself is a Google Doc only Grasslands students can open, so the date you need is the one the school sets. Ask the BCHS office in the fall.
description: A trades award tied to courses you have to have already taken. Applicants must be in good standing with Brooks Composite High School, must have taken Construction at the 10, 20 and 30 levels, and must plan to pursue an apprenticeship in the trades. The course requirement means this is not something to discover in your final semester; the qualifying work happens across three years of CTS courses.
metaDetail: Needs Construction 10, 20 and 30 already done.

title: Ashton Moen Memorial Scholarship
audience: Members of the BCHS band program
notes: The handbook publishes no closing date for this award. Applications are collected by Brooks Composite High School rather than by the sponsor, and the form itself is a Google Doc only Grasslands students can open, so the date you need is the one the school sets. Ask the BCHS office in the fall.
description: Established by the Newell County Band Association in memory of Ashton Moen, a member of the Brooks Composite High School band department, to keep her memory alive in the program she belonged to. The association names kindness and selflessness as the qualities she was known for and as what the award is meant to recognise, so band membership is the eligibility and character is the criterion.
metaDetail: From the Newell County Band Association.

title: MNP LLP Scholarship
audience: Grade 12 students entering a business program
notes: The handbook publishes no closing date for this award. Applications are collected by Brooks Composite High School rather than by the sponsor, and the form itself is a Google Doc only Grasslands students can open, so the date you need is the one the school sets. Ask the BCHS office in the fall.
description: MNP funds this for current Grade 12 students who plan to enroll in a business program at a post-secondary institution in the fall immediately following graduation. The application asks about your post-secondary plans, your school and community involvement, and your personal interests, so it is a written application rather than a marks cutoff. The immediate-fall condition rules out a gap year.
metaDetail: You must start the program the fall after grad.

title: Jimmy Bonora Memorial Trades Award
audience: Grade 12 students enrolled in a certified trades program
notes: Submitted to Student Services at BCHS by May 15, not to the sponsor. Your application has to include at least one letter from a BCHS staff member supporting your enthusiasm for the trades, and the name of the program you are entering. Jimmy Bonora's wife and two children choose the recipient.
description: A single $1,000 award in memory of Jimmy Bonora, a BCHS graduate who apprenticed with his father as an electrician and went on to run Mario's Electric in Brooks. It goes to a Grade 12 student showing a positive attitude, motivation and dedication to a trades education. The one hard requirement is enrolment: you must be in, or able to prove you are entering, a certified trades program in Canada.
metaDetail: Needs a staff letter backing your trades plan.

title: Techmation Trades Scholarship
audience: BCHS Grade 12 students entering a certified trades program
notes: The handbook publishes no closing date for this award. Applications are collected by Brooks Composite High School rather than by the sponsor, and the form itself is a Google Doc only Grasslands students can open, so the date you need is the one the school sets. Ask the BCHS office in the fall.
description: Techmation puts $1,500 behind a Grade 12 student showing a positive attitude, motivation, and dedication to advancing their education through a trades program. Applicants have to be current Grade 12 students at Brooks Composite High School and either enrolled in a certified trades program in Canada or accepted for the 2026-2027 school year. At $1,500 it is the largest single Brooks trades award in this handbook.
metaDetail: The largest single Brooks trades award.

title: Brooks Rotary Club Pathfinder Scholarship
audience: First Nations, Métis and Inuit graduates in Brooks and County of Newell
notes: The handbook publishes no closing date for this award. It is open past Brooks Composite itself, so if you graduate from another high school in the area, ask your own office how it collects the application; the BCHS handbook is where the criteria are written down.
description: A $1,000 award from the Brooks Rotary Club for a graduating student who self-identifies as First Nations, Métis, or Inuit. It is written to recognise community-building contributions, particularly within Indigenous communities, and names leadership, cultural pride, resilience and kindness as what it is looking for. It is open to students graduating from any high school in the City of Brooks or the County of Newell who are entering college, university, or technical training, so technical training counts here as much as a degree does.
metaDetail: Technical training counts, not just a degree.

title: Pat Zukowski Trades Scholarship
audience: Grasslands Grade 12 students in a certified trades program
notes: The handbook publishes no closing date for this award. Applications go through your Grasslands school rather than to the sponsor, and the form is a Google Doc only Grasslands students can open, so ask your school office in the fall for the date it is collecting by.
description: Five scholarships of $1,000 each go every year to Grasslands Public Schools Grade 12 students who are enrolled in, or can prove enrolment in, a certified trades program in Canada. Preference goes to students engaged in dual credit trades programming or CTS trades programming. Pat Zukowski was a Grasslands graduate, a welder, and for four decades a co-owner of an oilfield construction company; he was worried about the shrinking number of tradespeople locally, and five awards a year is a deliberately wide net.
metaDetail: Five awards a year; dual credit preferred.

title: Ryder Ferguson Memorial Scholarship
audience: Grade 12 students entering automotive, heavy equipment or ag technician programs
notes: The handbook publishes no closing date for this award. Applications are collected by Brooks Composite High School rather than by the sponsor, and the form itself is a Google Doc only Grasslands students can open, so the date you need is the one the school sets. Ask the BCHS office in the fall.
description: A $1,000 scholarship in memory of Ryder Ferguson, who would have graduated in June 2026. It supports a graduating Grade 12 student who shows dedication to hands-on work and technical skill and wants to build a future in the Automotive, Heavy Equipment, or Agricultural Service Technician programs. The three named programs are the eligibility; this is not a general trades award.

title: Constable David Wynn Memorial Award
audience: St. Albert graduates entering policing, law, medicine or emergency services
notes: The foundation writes the criteria but does not collect the application; your high school counsellor does, and each school sets its own cutoff. The date shown is the earliest of the ones published, so treat it as the safe one to work back from.
description: Named for the RCMP constable killed in St. Albert in 2015, and written around what he believed: that every young person deserves a leg up and deserves recognition for service. It asks for a 65% average, a record of volunteer or leadership service in school, community or international programs, and two letters of reference to back that record up. The fields named are police work, EMT, paramedic, law, military, forensic science and medicine, including nursing, pharmacy and lab tech, though the wording is deliberately not limited to them. Consideration is given to students from financially challenged families. It is offered at Bellerose, Paul Kane, St. Albert Catholic, Outreach and St. Gabriel, which is the widest reach of any award on this list.
metaDetail: Reachable from five St. Albert schools.

title: Jaxon Joseph For the Love of the Game Award
audience: Grade 12 hockey players at Paul Kane, Bellerose or St. Albert Catholic
notes: The date here is Paul Kane's April 10. Bellerose collects the same award until June 1 and the other schools set their own, so the deadline you are held to is your own school's, not the one printed here. Ask your counsellor which applies to you.
description: One of four awards the families created after the 2018 Humboldt Broncos bus crash, which killed four young men from St. Albert. This one is for players who love the game itself rather than players at the top of the scoring sheet: Jaxon Joseph did not always make the top AAA team and kept pushing anyway, and the award is written around that. You need a 70% average through high school, a commitment to community through service or volunteering, and participation in hockey inside or outside school. The application is a short essay or a video of up to five minutes, a coach's reference, a transcript, and proof of post-secondary acceptance.
metaDetail: Needs a 70% average and a coach's reference.

title: Conner Lukan Tighten Your Skates Award
audience: Grade 12 hockey players entering athletic therapy or physiotherapy
notes: The date here is Paul Kane's April 10. Bellerose collects the same award until June 1 and the other schools set their own, so the deadline you are held to is your own school's, not the one printed here. Ask your counsellor which applies to you.
description: A second of the four Humboldt memorial awards, this one tied to a field of study. It goes to a student heading for athletic therapy, physiotherapy, or another career that helps heal the human body, which is a much narrower gate than the hockey requirement beside it. You need a 70% average, service or volunteer involvement, demonstrated leadership, and participation in hockey. Conner Lukan spent his summers training on a dirt road by the lake at Slave Lake, and the award is built around that kind of dedication rather than around results.
metaDetail: Field of study is the narrow part, not the sport.

title: Logan Hunter Youth Leadership Award
audience: Grade 12 hockey players who coach or volunteer with younger kids
notes: The date here is Paul Kane's April 10. Bellerose collects the same award until June 1 and the other schools set their own, so the deadline you are held to is your own school's, not the one printed here. Ask your counsellor which applies to you.
description: The third Humboldt memorial award, and the one that asks for what you have done for younger players. Logan Hunter wanted to be a teacher and spent his time helping young people as a volunteer and a coach, so the criteria ask for excellence in hockey over more than two years, character and respect for coaches, and support and involvement of youth through volunteering or teaching. A 70% average is required, along with a commitment to training or personal fitness. The submission is an essay or a video of up to five minutes, a coach's reference, and a transcript.
metaDetail: Wants two or more years of hockey and youth work.

title: Stephen Wack Confidence to Follow Your Heart Award
audience: Grade 10, 11 and 12 hockey players with an 80% average
notes: The date here is Paul Kane's April 10. Bellerose collects the same award until June 1 and the other schools set their own, so the deadline you are held to is your own school's, not the one printed here. Ask your counsellor which applies to you.
description: The last of the four Humboldt awards and the one built differently from the others. It is open from grade 10, it asks for an 80% average rather than 70%, and it is meant to fund personal growth in any area the recipient chooses: higher education, sport, hobbies, training, classes, or equipment. Stephen Wack was an honours student and a self-taught videographer as well as a defenceman, and priority goes to students who play defence. The criteria ask for extraordinary commitment to personal growth and an exemplary work ethic on and off the ice, not for a points total.
metaDetail: Open from grade 10, and the money need not go to tuition.

title: Shea-Lynn McGaw Be Strong Never Give Up Award
audience: Graduating volleyball players at Bellerose, Paul Kane or St. Albert Catholic
notes: The date here is Paul Kane's April 10. Bellerose collects the same award until June 1 and the other schools set their own, so the deadline you are held to is your own school's, not the one printed here. Ask your counsellor which applies to you.
description: For a student-athlete in their graduation year who plays high school or club volleyball and carries a never give up attitude onto the court. The award says plainly that the recipient may not be the most skilled player on the team, and asks instead for strength of character, persistence against challenges, dedication to the team, and encouragement of teammates. Applicants can put themselves forward or be nominated by someone else. The money has to be used toward post-secondary tuition or associated costs within two years of graduating, which is an unusually long window.
metaDetail: You can be nominated rather than apply yourself.

title: Patricia Trudeau Scholarship
audience: St. Albert students entering fine arts, design or musical theatre
notes: The date here is Paul Kane's April 10. Bellerose collects the same award until June 1 and the other schools set their own, so the deadline you are held to is your own school's, not the one printed here. Ask your counsellor which applies to you.
description: One fund, but the criteria are written separately for each school that offers it. At Bellerose it goes to a student entering fine arts, musical theatre or design studies who has completed a 30 level course in arts, communications or musical theatre. At Paul Kane it splits into two Art and Design awards for graduating students with demonstrated financial need who finished Art 30, Art 31, Design Studies 30 or Communication Technology 30. At St. Albert Catholic it covers art, drama, musical theatre and music, and also asks for commitment to the arts outside school hours. Outreach and St. Gabriel run their own versions through administration.
metaDetail: Criteria differ by school; Paul Kane's version weighs financial need.

title: Rouse Family Relentless Award
audience: Graduating students who have come through serious adversity
notes: You do not apply for this one directly; the school nominates. That makes the useful step telling the staff who would put your name forward that you are interested, well before the grad awards are decided.
description: For a graduating student who has kept going through real difficulty: the criteria talk about resilience, grit, a steady work ethic, and belief in your own ability to get past an obstacle. There is no marks floor and no field of study attached, which makes it one of the few awards here that a student with an interrupted or difficult few years can genuinely win. It is offered at Bellerose, Paul Kane, St. Albert Catholic, Outreach and St. Gabriel.
metaDetail: Offered at five St. Albert schools.

title: Erin James Scholarship
audience: Grade 12 Bellerose students committed to their studies and their school
notes: No closing date is published for this one. It is handled inside the school rather than by the sponsor, so the date you need is whatever your counsellor or the student centre is working to this year.
description: Erin James graduated from the Bellerose International Baccalaureate programme in 2000 and went on to a Bachelor of Arts and a public relations diploma. The scholarship in her name is presented annually to a grade 12 Bellerose student, and says outright that the recipient is not required to have the highest academic average. What it asks for instead is commitment to your academics, a contribution to the Bellerose community, and compassion, kindness and generosity toward others.
metaDetail: States outright that the top average is not the point.

title: Stanley Dennis We Believe In You Award
audience: Paul Kane students in grades 10 to 12 who are working hard to get ahead
notes: Paul Kane collects this one and its handout gives April 10 as the date, with no year attached, so it is an annual cutoff rather than a one-off. The handout also says every detail in it is subject to change, so confirm the date with Student Services before you plan around it.
description: Stanley Dennis struggled in school and had great potential, and this award exists to tell a student in the same position that somebody believes in them. It is for a Paul Kane student who is working hard to get ahead, and it is open from grade 10 rather than only at graduation. It is one of three awards the Stanley Dennis Memorial Fund pays for at Paul Kane, and the only one of the three with no field of study attached to it.
metaDetail: Written for the student who struggles and keeps going.

title: Katherine Dennis Scholarship
audience: Grade 12 Paul Kane students entering fine or performing arts
notes: Paul Kane collects this one and its handout gives April 10 as the date, with no year attached, so it is an annual cutoff rather than a one-off. The handout also says every detail in it is subject to change, so confirm the date with Student Services before you plan around it.
description: The second of the three awards the Stanley Dennis Memorial Fund pays for at Paul Kane. It goes to a grade 12 student heading into media and visual arts or performing arts, and the recipient has to provide proof of enrolment in a fine arts or similar degree program at a recognised post-secondary institution. The proof requirement means this is settled after you have an acceptance in hand, not before.
metaDetail: Needs proof of enrolment in a fine arts program.

title: Christopher Dennis Scholarship
audience: Grade 12 Paul Kane students entering commerce or technology
notes: Paul Kane collects this one and its handout gives April 10 as the date, with no year attached, so it is an annual cutoff rather than a one-off. The handout also says every detail in it is subject to change, so confirm the date with Student Services before you plan around it.
description: The third award from the Stanley Dennis Memorial Fund at Paul Kane, this one for a grade 12 student pursuing business or technologies. Paul Kane's own handout reads the technologies half broadly: computer science, engineering, environmental technologies, biotechnology and manufacturing technologies all count. The recipient has to show proof of enrolment in a Bachelor of Commerce or a technologies degree program at a recognised institution.
metaDetail: Covers engineering and biotech, not just commerce.

title: KDM Helping Hands Community Spirit Award
audience: Outreach and St. Gabriel students aged 18 or under with a 60% average
notes: No closing date is published for this one. It is handled inside the school rather than by the sponsor, so the date you need is whatever your counsellor or the student centre is working to this year.
description: Established by the KDM Helping Hands Charity for students in the Primary Outreach program at St. Gabriel Education Centre and St. Albert Outreach High School. The bar is set where those students are: 18 or under, an overall average of 60%, and no requirement to be a resident of St. Albert or the surrounding area. It goes to a student who has shown perseverance in finishing their studies and who supports their family, school and community through what they actually do. Awards written for outreach students are rare in Alberta, and this is one of very few.
metaDetail: Does not require you to live in St. Albert.

title: Coach Rowein Alumni Basketball Award
audience: Greater St. Albert area students who played senior basketball at Morinville
notes: No closing date is published for this one. It is handled inside the school rather than by the sponsor, so the date you need is whatever your counsellor or the student centre is working to this year.
description: Open to a student in their last year at any greater St. Albert area high school, with highest priority going to students enrolled at Morinville Community High School who played on the senior basketball team there. You need verified acceptance from your chosen post-secondary school, demonstrated teamwork and leadership on the court and in the school, dedication and perseverance in your studies, and a written reference showing you are held in high regard by teachers, teammates or a coach. The priority wording means students outside Morinville can apply but should read the odds honestly.
metaDetail: Open area-wide, with Morinville players first in line.

title: Gagné Family Music Scholarship
audience: Young musicians playing traditional Canadian fiddle
notes: No closing date is published for this one. It is handled inside the school rather than by the sponsor, so the date you need is whatever your counsellor or the student centre is working to this year.
description: Created by the Gagné family in honour of their grandmother Delia, whose fiddle playing shaped the family, and dedicated to keeping traditional Canadian fiddle music alive. It is presented each year through the St. Albert Rotary Music Festival to young musicians who show passion, talent and commitment to carrying those traditions forward. The money is meant for lessons, camps, instruments or musical development rather than tuition, which makes it usable well before you graduate.
metaDetail: Can fund lessons, camps or an instrument.

title: Jackie Heitzman Rose Bowl Award
audience: The best overall performer at the St. Albert Rotary Music Festival
notes: You reach this one by entering the festival rather than by filing a scholarship application, so the date that matters is the festival's entry deadline. The festival runs in the spring; check its own schedule in the fall.
description: Established in memory of Jackie Heitzman, an active member of the St. Albert community, to support people heading into careers in music. It is presented each year at the St. Albert Rotary Music Festival to the best overall performing artist, which makes it one of the very few awards on this list you win by performing rather than by filling in a form.
metaDetail: Won by performing, not by applying.

title: Adam Stychin Be Positive Award
audience: Paul Kane students who completed Construction and Fabrication 30
notes: Paul Kane collects this one and its handout gives April 10 as the date, with no year attached, so it is an annual cutoff rather than a one-off. The handout also says every detail in it is subject to change, so confirm the date with Student Services before you plan around it.
description: Named to honour Adam Stychin, who intended to follow his love of woodworking into a career as an architect and to build a bee farm. It goes to two students who completed Construction and Fabrication 30, showed exceptional kindness and a willingness to help others, and took part in school events. The course requirement is the hard gate; the rest is character, which makes it a genuine shot for a shop student whose transcript is unremarkable.
metaDetail: Two awards, and kindness is an explicit criterion.

title: Brostrom-Maltby Memorial Award
audience: Two graduating Paul Kane students with visible school spirit
notes: Paul Kane collects this one and its handout gives April 10 as the date, with no year attached, so it is an annual cutoff rather than a one-off. The handout also says every detail in it is subject to change, so confirm the date with Student Services before you plan around it.
description: In memory of Yvonne Brostrom and Andrew Maltby, two Paul Kane students from the class of 1975. It goes to two graduating students who are involved in school activities and shine with school spirit, and the founders ask specifically for students who show a positive attitude toward friends, teachers and parents. There is no marks requirement and no field of study, which is rare among the graduating awards at this school.
metaDetail: Two awards, judged on attitude rather than marks.

title: CUPE Local 1099 St. Albert Public High School Scholarship
audience: Any St. Albert public high school graduate willing to write 750 words
notes: July 30 is the date CUPE gives, well after the April cluster at the school, so this one is still live over the summer when most of the others have closed.
description: Two $1,000 scholarships from CUPE Local 1099, open to any student graduating from a St. Albert public high school. The application is proof of enrolment in any post-secondary program plus an original essay of at least 750 words answering one question: how has the history of unionized workers helped shape Canada. There is no average requirement and no field restriction, so the essay is the whole competition.
metaDetail: Two awards of $1,000, decided on one essay.

title: Curtains Up Scholarship
audience: Grade 12 Paul Kane students in the theatre arts program
notes: Paul Kane collects this one and its handout gives April 10 as the date, with no year attached, so it is an annual cutoff rather than a one-off. The handout also says every detail in it is subject to change, so confirm the date with Student Services before you plan around it.
description: For a grade 12 student who has made a significant contribution to the theatre arts program at Paul Kane. It is judged on what you put into the program rather than on marks or on a plan to study theatre after graduation, so backstage and production work counts as much as performing does.
metaDetail: Judged on what you gave the theatre program.

title: Joan Trettler Award
audience: Graduating St. Albert public students with a leadership record
notes: The date here is Paul Kane's April 10. Bellerose collects the same award until June 1 and the other schools set their own, so the deadline you are held to is your own school's, not the one printed here. Ask your counsellor which applies to you.
description: For a graduating student described as well rounded and community minded, showing outstanding leadership in student activities. It runs at both Paul Kane and Bellerose, and the applicant must have accepted registration at a post-secondary institution, so an offer alone is not enough. Bellerose puts its own cutoff at May 1 while Paul Kane collects with its April cluster.
metaDetail: Offered at both Paul Kane and Bellerose.

title: Kinsmen Club of St. Albert Service Award
audience: Grade 12 students with a record of service volunteering
notes: The date here is Paul Kane's April 10. Bellerose collects the same award until June 1 and the other schools set their own, so the deadline you are held to is your own school's, not the one printed here. Ask your counsellor which applies to you.
description: The St. Albert Kinsmen recognise students who have committed to their school or community through service-oriented volunteerism. Successful students get $500 and a plaque, and the applicant must have accepted registration at a post-secondary institution. It runs at both Paul Kane and Bellerose, and unlike most of the service awards here it names a figure rather than leaving it open.
metaDetail: Comes with a plaque as well as the money.

title: Paul Kane Global Languages Award
audience: Paul Kane students taking two or more languages to the 30 level
notes: Paul Kane collects this one and its handout gives April 10 as the date, with no year attached, so it is an annual cutoff rather than a one-off. The handout also says every detail in it is subject to change, so confirm the date with Student Services before you plan around it.
description: For a student who has shown exceptional commitment to two or more languages other than English at the 30 level, and who demonstrates leadership in using those languages outside the classroom. The out of class requirement is what separates this from the school's Japanese 30, Spanish 30 and French 30 prizes, which are decided on marks alone and need no application.
metaDetail: Wants languages used outside the classroom too.

title: Paul Kane Principal's Award
audience: A grade 12 Paul Kane student with three years of contribution
notes: Paul Kane collects this one and its handout gives April 10 as the date, with no year attached, so it is an annual cutoff rather than a one-off. The handout also says every detail in it is subject to change, so confirm the date with Student Services before you plan around it.
description: Presented to the grade 12 student who best exemplifies the school's own acronym: perseverance, knowledge, honour and service. The criteria ask for significant contributions to Paul Kane activities and events across all three years, so this is not something a strong final year can win on its own.
metaDetail: Wants three years of involvement, not one.

title: Paul Kane Unsung Hero Scholarship
audience: A graduating Paul Kane student chosen by student vote
notes: Paul Kane collects this one and its handout gives April 10 as the date, with no year attached, so it is an annual cutoff rather than a one-off. The handout also says every detail in it is subject to change, so confirm the date with Student Services before you plan around it.
description: For a graduating student who has given outstanding extracurricular service to the school and the community, honouring the legacy of Mr. Dale Smith's leadership at Paul Kane. What makes it unusual is the selection: a student vote decides the winner, not a committee, which means it rewards the kind of contribution your classmates actually noticed.
metaDetail: The winner is decided by a vote of the students.

title: PKHS Character Award
audience: Two graduating Paul Kane students with a 75% average
notes: Paul Kane collects this one and its handout gives April 10 as the date, with no year attached, so it is an annual cutoff rather than a one-off. The handout also says every detail in it is subject to change, so confirm the date with Student Services before you plan around it.
description: For two graduating students who persevered through high school while demonstrating leadership and service at school and in the community. The marks bar is set with the school's own Standard of Excellence calculation, and winners need an average of at least 75% by that measure, which is a real floor but a modest one next to the school's honours awards.
metaDetail: Two awards, with a 75% floor.

title: Rotary Club of St. Albert Scholarship
audience: Grade 12 students entering arts, trades, technology, business or French study
notes: The date here is Paul Kane's April 10. Bellerose collects the same award until June 1 and the other schools set their own, so the deadline you are held to is your own school's, not the one printed here. Ask your counsellor which applies to you.
description: Formerly the Roy Swanson Memorial, this is a $1,000 scholarship for a grade 12 student going on to post-secondary study in fine arts, trades, technology, business, or study in French. Bellerose's version of the criteria sets a minimum 65% overall average and asks for above-average community service in the school or the community. The five eligible fields are unusually wide for a service club award, and trades sit in the list on equal footing with business.
metaDetail: A 65% floor and five eligible fields.

title: Rotary Club of St. Albert Service Above Self Award
audience: St. Albert students in grades 10 to 12 who volunteer
notes: The date here is Paul Kane's April 10. Bellerose collects the same award until June 1 and the other schools set their own, so the deadline you are held to is your own school's, not the one printed here. Ask your counsellor which applies to you.
description: Up to twelve of these go to St. Albert high school students who volunteer at school and in the community in a service or leadership role. Each recipient gets $250 and, separately, the chance to apply for a $250 grant toward their next local or international project. It is open from grade 10, and twelve awards against one city's students is among the best odds on this list.
metaDetail: Up to 12 awards, plus a $250 project grant.

title: Rotary Club of St. Albert Stephen Barr Memorial Award
audience: St. Albert students entering visual arts or architecture
notes: May 31 is the date Paul Kane publishes for this one, six weeks later than its main April cluster. Bellerose runs it through the student centre on its own schedule.
description: A $1,000 award for a St. Albert student who has completed or is enrolled in the Alberta Education Art 30 curriculum and is applying to post-secondary study in visual arts or architecture. Architecture sitting alongside visual arts is what makes this worth reading twice: a student heading into a design or architecture degree rarely finds an arts award that will take them.
metaDetail: Architecture counts here, not only studio art.

title: Ryan Burak Memorial Award
audience: A graduating Paul Kane senior team athlete whose marks improved
notes: Paul Kane collects this one and its handout gives April 10 as the date, with no year attached, so it is an annual cutoff rather than a one-off. The handout also says every detail in it is subject to change, so confirm the date with Student Services before you plan around it.
description: For a graduating male student on one of Paul Kane's senior athletic teams who has improved his academic standing while at the school and is going on to post-secondary, preferably in business. Improvement rather than a high average is what is being measured, which makes this reachable for an athlete whose grade 10 year was weak.
metaDetail: Rewards an improved transcript, not a high one.

title: Shayne H. Page Memorial Scholarship
audience: Paul Kane graduates who spent three years at Lorne Akins Junior High
notes: Paul Kane collects this one and its handout gives April 10 as the date, with no year attached, so it is an annual cutoff rather than a one-off. The handout also says every detail in it is subject to change, so confirm the date with Student Services before you plan around it.
description: One of the narrowest awards in St. Albert. The recipient has to be a Paul Kane grade 12 graduate who attended Lorne Akins Junior High School for three years and Paul Kane for three years, and who is registered full time at a post-secondary institution inside Alberta. Two school histories and a province, all three of which have to line up, so the pool in a given year is small.
metaDetail: Needs three years at Lorne Akins and three at PK.

title: Shirley Brauer Award for Women in Science

title: St. Albert Breakfast Lions Club We Serve Award

metaDetail: Also called the Lion Gerry Gorgichuk Memorial Bursary.

title: St. Albert Cosmopolitan Club Art Nixon Construction and Fabrication Award

description: For a grade 10 student who has shown proficiency and skill in construction and fabrication courses. metaDetail: A grade 10 award, which is rare in the trades.

title: St. Albert Cosmopolitan Club Joe May Poetry Award of Excellence

title: St. Albert Host Lions Club Legacy Award

metaDetail: A September date makes it live after graduation.

title: Cpl. Jordan Anderson Memorial Award

title: Cultural Enrichment Award

metaDetail: Needs three years of U15AAA hockey in St. Albert.

title: Stanley Haroun Award

metaDetail: Rewards three years of improvement at Bellerose.

title: Workun Garrick Partnership Award

title: St. Albert Legion Poppy Fund Bursary

metaDetail: Eligibility runs through a family service record.

title: St. Albert Minor Hockey Scholarship
audience: St. Albert U18 Interlock players and U18 officials

description: Up to two $1,000 scholarships a year for players in the U18 Interlock program, plus one $1,000 scholarship for a U18 official, all for students continuing to a post-secondary institution. metaDetail: One of the three awards is for officials.

title: St. Albert Young Artist Legacy Award
audience: St. Albert residents aged 13 to 21 pursuing a career in the arts
notes: The City runs this as a civic grant with an intake rather than a fixed graduation deadline, and it will not cover post-secondary tuition, equipment purchases, rental fees or studio time. description: A City of St. Albert grant of up to $500 for an individual or $1,000 for a youth group, open to St. Albert residents aged 13 to 21 who are pursuing a career in the arts. The age range starting at 13 makes this one of the earliest pieces of arts money in the province, and the application is reviewed by a committee of the City's Arts Development Advisory Committee.
metaDetail: Ages 13 to 21, and it funds training, not tuition.

title: Spruce Grove Chamber of Commerce Award

description: The Spruce Grove Chamber of Commerce funds this for a graduating student who has given service to the school and the community. title: Darren Schellenberger L.I.F.E. Award

metaDetail: Nominated by ten classmates, then decided by class vote.

title: French Immersion Leadership Award

description: The immersion counterpart of the Canadian Parents for French award beside it, also funded by the CPF Parkland Chapter and also explicit that academic marks are not a criterion. metaDetail: Marks are explicitly not a criterion; leadership in promoting French is.

notes: Spruce Grove Composite gates all of its grade 12 awards behind one Awards Application Form plus a Teacher Endorsement Form, both filed with Student Services. title: Kaleb Price Memorial Scholarship

description: Funded by the Price family for an outstanding grade 12 student who best exemplifies kindness, altruism, light to others, exuberance and benevolence. Award it runs on a nomination supported by ten graduating classmates and one teacher, with the graduating class voting to choose from the nominees.

title: Orest Haydey Connie Archer Panther Auxiliary Award

metaDetail: Two awards, one male and one female.

title: Parkland School Division Citizenship Scholarship
audience: Parkland students with a 70 to 79.5% average and no other major award

The weighted average in all grade 12 courses has to sit between 70 and 79.5%, so a strong transcript rules you out, and you must not have received any other major school-based award or scholarship. Add good citizenship, participation in the local and school communities, an attendance rate above 80%, and enrolment at a post-secondary institution. It is written for the solid middle of the class, which is exactly where scholarship money is usually thinnest.
metaDetail: Ten awards, and a high average disqualifies you.

title: PEP Award

description: Funded by Spruce Grove Composite itself for a student with a learning disability who is going on to further study and who demonstrates performance, effort and persistence. metaDetail: One of very few Alberta awards written for this.

title: Robert Chamney Memorial Scholarship

metaDetail: Preference to students who overcame significant obstacles.

title: Border Paving Award

metaDetail: Decided on blended English, Math and Physics marks.

title: Capital Plumbing and Heating Scholarship

The tools are the part worth noticing, because a first-year apprentice buying their own kit is facing a real cost that a cash award of this size would barely cover on its own.
metaDetail: Comes with tools as well as the money.

title: Constituency of Lac Ste. Anne-Parkland Award for Leadership in Business

notes: Memorial Composite does not asterisk this one, which in its award list means there is no separate application to file; the school selects from the students in front of it. description: Presented by the Constituency of Lac Ste. Anne-Parkland to the student who best demonstrates the potential to be a leader in the business world. metaDetail: Judged on potential rather than on a transcript.

title: Constituency of Spruce Grove-Stony Plain Award for Leadership in Building a Better Community

description: Awarded each year by the Constituency of Spruce Grove-Stony Plain to the graduating student who best demonstrates a commitment to social activism. A single event will not read well here; a campaign you kept going will.
metaDetail: Wants sustained activism, not a single project.

metaDetail: Needs a 75% grade 12 average plus school commitment.

title: Dr. Dekterov Health Care Professionals Award

description: Funded by Dentistry by Dekterov and granted to a graduating Memorial Composite student entering a post-secondary program related to health sciences. title: Elizabeth Spychka Citizenship Scholarship

metaDetail: Preference to students who helped run graduation.

title: Hawkings Tinney LLP Commerce Award

metaDetail: Wants prior hands-on agricultural experience.

title: Meridian Masonic Lodge Bursary
