metaDetail: Needs all three high school mechanics levels.

title: Green and Gold Athletic Scholarships
audience: Memorial Composite athletes with a 70% average and two years on a team
notes: Memorial Composite does not asterisk this one, which in its award list means there is no separate application to file; the school selects from the students in front of it. Making sure the department knows you want it is the step that is actually available to you.
description: Memorial Composite fund two of these at $1,000 each for athletes who are well rounded and community minded, with a positive attitude, unselfishness, responsibility, coachability, leadership and goal setting. The hard requirements are an overall average of at least 70% in grade 12, involvement on at least one school athletic team in two high school years with one of them being grade 12, and involvement in Green and Gold fundraising while at the school. That last one is easy to miss and cannot be fixed late.
metaDetail: Two awards, and fundraising involvement is required.

title: Spruce Grove and District Agricultural Heritage Society Student Scholarship
audience: Tri-Region residents in an agriculture-related program, any year
notes: Applications go by email to the society rather than through a school, and it says late or incomplete applications will not be considered. Note that the society's own page now says $1,000 each; the $750 figure that appears on a school scholarship page and in older coverage is out of date.
description: Two scholarships of $1,000 each from the Spruce Grove and District Agricultural Society, for students enrolled in an agriculture-related field of study at an accredited college, university or trade school. Two things make this wider than a typical graduation award: any year of study qualifies, not just first year, and past applicants and recipients are allowed to apply again. You have to be a resident of the Tri-Region, meaning Parkland County, Spruce Grove or Stony Plain.
metaDetail: Open to any year of study, and past recipients may reapply.

title: Leduc County Agricultural Service Board Bursary
audience: Leduc County residents in an agriculture-related program
notes: The county's page gives a mailing and email route for this one but prints no closing date, unlike the two scholarships beside it. Ask Agricultural Services in Nisku for the current date rather than assuming it shares their October 31.
description: Five bursaries of $1,000 each go every year to post-secondary students in an agriculture-related program. You have to be a Leduc County resident or the child of one, and the application is a form, proof of acceptance such as an acceptance letter or course registration, and a 500-word essay on your future aspirations and how your education supports them. Greater consideration goes to applicants who have not received it before, so it is worth applying in a year when you think the field is strong.
metaDetail: Five bursaries, and repeat winners are deprioritised.

title: Albert and Maria Rimer Memorial Scholarship
audience: Warburg High School graduates entering agriculture or health sciences
notes: Leduc County takes this one directly rather than through a school, and the successful applicant has to supply a social insurance number and birthdate afterwards. Financial need is weighed alongside the stated criteria.
description: Bert Rimer gave Leduc County $50,000 in memory of his parents to fund this for Warburg High School graduates. The amount varies year to year but will be at least $1,000. The primary target is a post-secondary major in agriculture or agricultural food, with secondary consideration for applicants in health sciences and medicine, and you cannot have received it before. Warburg is a village of a few hundred people, so the field this competes against is very small.
metaDetail: One school, and previous recipients cannot reapply.

title: George L. Saubak Memorial Fund Scholarship
audience: Calmar, Thorsby and Warburg graduates entering a medical field
notes: Leduc County takes this one directly rather than through a school, and the successful applicant has to supply a social insurance number and birthdate afterwards. Financial need is weighed alongside the stated criteria.
description: Katie Dringenberg left Leduc County $20,000 to start this fund, asking that it go to a graduate of Calmar High School, Thorsby High School or Warburg High School. It is awarded annually to a post-secondary student with a declared major in a medical field, and the county names nursing, dentistry, pharmacy and veterinary medicine as examples rather than limits. Previous recipients are not eligible again.
metaDetail: Nursing, dentistry, pharmacy and veterinary all count.

title: Ambassador Scholarship
audience: Black Gold graduates who finished high school in three years
notes: This one closes on September 10 following graduation, which is after most students have already started post-secondary, so it is easy to forget about. Applications go to your principal, who submits the school's candidate to the superintendent by September 15.
description: Funded by Cory Bablitz, a Calmar Secondary graduate, for a Black Gold graduate continuing to post-secondary. You must have been enrolled at a Black Gold school for your grade twelve year and completed high school in three years, be accepted into a post-secondary program, and show genuine commitment across academics, sports in school or the community, and citizenship or volunteering. The application is a covering letter, a summary of all three areas, and three letters of reference, one for each.
metaDetail: Needs three reference letters, one for each criterion.

title: Greg Sylvester Memorial Scholarship
audience: Black Gold graduates studying history at Bishop's or Queen's
notes: Black Gold's own division-managed scholarship summary is where the criteria and the date come from, and the date it gives is a bare day with no year, so it repeats. The summary was last updated in April 2025, so confirm the amount with the division before counting on it.
description: Funded by the estate of Gregory Garth Sylvester and paid in two halves, $500 in September and $500 in February on continued registration. The requirement is unusually specific: acceptance into Bishop's or Queen's University with history as a major area of study, plus a year at a Black Gold high school including grade twelve. The application is a letter of recommendation from a teacher or principal and a short account of why you are pursuing history. The deadline is July 15 of any year after you finish grade 12, so a student who switches into history later can still apply.
metaDetail: You can apply in any year after grade 12, not just the first.

title: Eric and Agnes Dixon Scholarship
audience: Black Gold graduates majoring in music at an Alberta institution
notes: The deadline is September 15 after you finish grade 12, which lands after most students have moved. If the music award goes unclaimed in a year, the fund instead pays two $500 Scandinavian Studies scholarships the following year, for study of a Scandinavian language.
description: A music scholarship paid $500 in October and $500 in February on continued registration. You have to be accepted into a post-secondary program in Alberta with music as a major area of study, and to have spent at least a year at a Black Gold high school including grade twelve. The application is a letter of recommendation from a music teacher or principal plus a short account of your musical background and why you are continuing in music.
metaDetail: Paid in two halves on continued registration.

title: Kevin Gaetz Award
audience: Black Gold graduates whose finances would otherwise block post-secondary
notes: Black Gold's own division-managed scholarship summary is where the criteria and the date come from, and the date it gives is a bare day with no year, so it repeats. The summary was last updated in April 2025, so confirm the amount with the division before counting on it.
description: Three recipients a year at $6,000 each, held in perpetuity through the Edmonton Community Foundation and paid in two halves: $3,000 when granted and $3,000 on confirmation of a completed first semester and continued enrolment. The qualifying condition is financial need that would restrict your ability to pursue post-secondary education at all. The application is a form, a letter of introduction addressing the criteria, a reference letter from an authority figure outside your immediate family, a current transcript, and a preliminary acceptance letter. At $6,000 this is the largest locally funded award in the Leduc area by a wide margin.
metaDetail: Three awards a year, the largest local award in Leduc.

title: Richard Anderson Scholarship
audience: John Maland High School graduates in Devon with a 70% GPA
notes: Black Gold's own division-managed scholarship summary is where the criteria and the date come from, and the date it gives is a bare day with no year, so it repeats. The summary was last updated in April 2025, so confirm the amount with the division before counting on it.
description: Two awards of $2,500 each at John Maland High School in Devon, established in 2024. You need a GPA of 70%, you must meet the entrance requirements for post-secondary study, and you must have financial need that would restrict your ability to go. The application is a form, a letter of introduction, a reference letter from an authority figure outside your immediate family, a transcript, and a preliminary acceptance letter. The selection committee is made up of staff from the school itself.
metaDetail: Two awards, decided by the school's own staff.

title: Bruce and Mary Marsh Education Scholarship
audience: Leduc Composite graduates in their second year of a BEd
notes: This is not a graduation award. You apply in September of your second year in the Bachelor of Education program, so a Leduc Composite graduate needs to remember it a full year after leaving. The selection committee meets before October 15.
description: Mary Marsh established this in Leduc for a graduate of Leduc Composite High School who has reached the second year of a Bachelor of Education program at an Alberta university, preferably with a major in music. It pays $1,200 to a student in an elementary program with musical training and interest, or $1,000 for any other major within a BEd. The application is a personal letter, your grade 12 transcript, and the university transcript for the first year you have just finished.
metaDetail: Pays $1,200 for elementary with music, $1,000 otherwise.

title: Philip Ki Joon Oh Scholarship
audience: Beaumont Composite grade 12 students with a 70% average or better
notes: Beaumont Composite publishes a dated cutoff for this rather than a bare recurring day; the 2026 cycle closed May 8. Shortlisted candidates are interviewed by the awards committee, so budget time for that as well as for the form.
description: Three scholarships of $2,000 each at Beaumont Composite for outstanding all-round grade 12 students, and it is built in two levels so that a strong record without top marks still has a route in. Level I asks for an academic average of 80% or higher plus active participation on school or community sports teams, leadership and public speaking, and volunteering. Level II asks for a 70 to 79% average with contribution to school and community through service clubs, organisations and community activities, plus the same leadership and public speaking. Both require acceptance into a full-time program of at least two years.
metaDetail: Two entry levels, at 80% and at 70 to 79%.

title: Mathieu Lefevre Memorial Fund for Artists
audience: Beaumont Composite graduates entering visual or performing arts
notes: The division lists this one but publishes no criteria document and no date for it, so Beaumont Composite's student services is the only place to get either.
description: A $500 scholarship for École Secondaire Beaumont Composite High School students enrolling in post-secondary study of the visual or performing arts. One school and one field of study is about as narrow as an award gets, which is the reason to look at it: the number of Beaumont graduates going into an arts program in a given year is small.
metaDetail: Restricted to one school and one field.

title: Leduc Kinsmen Bursary
audience: Graduates of Leduc Composite, Ohpaho Secondary and Christ the King
notes: The Kinsmen publish a dated cutoff rather than a repeating one; the 2026 round closed June 2. Applications go by email or post to the club directly, and counsellors hold printed copies.
description: Established in 2020 as a Leduc Kinsmen legacy project and funded by the club's own fundraising. Three bursaries of $1,000 are granted, one each to a student from Leduc Composite High School, Ohpaho Secondary School and Christ the King School, so the three schools do not compete against each other. You need to be registering full time at a recognised post-secondary institution in your graduating year and be a Canadian citizen or permanent resident.
metaDetail: One award reserved for each of three schools.

title: Leduc Influencers Award
audience: Leduc youth aged 17 to 21 with a community record
notes: This runs through the City's Citizen Recognition Program on nominations rather than applications, so the move is getting someone to nominate you well before the March 31 date. It is a civic award with a bursary attached, not a school award.
description: The City of Leduc's Influencer awards celebrate the city's youth between the ages of 17 and 21 for outstanding contributions to the community, and winners receive a $1,000 bursary. The age range is what makes it different from everything else on this list: it stays open for several years after high school, so a graduate already at post-secondary is still eligible.
metaDetail: Ages 17 to 21, so it reaches past graduation.

title: Leduc Community Hospital Foundation Healthcare Studies Scholarship
audience: Leduc region students entering healthcare studies
notes: The foundation says applications are accepted in November with recipients announced the following March, but publishes no exact closing date, so watch its site through the fall. Its separate professional development awards are for working healthcare staff, not students.
description: The Leduc Community Hospital Foundation set up this programme in the fall of 2021 for people in the community with a commitment to healthcare through their chosen profession. Two scholarships of $1,000 each go annually to students from the Leduc region pursuing post-secondary healthcare-related studies. It is a small, locally funded programme against a small regional pool, which is the kind of ratio worth an application.
metaDetail: Two scholarships a year for the Leduc region.

title: Leduc Performing Arts and Cultural Foundation Media Arts Scholarship
audience: Leduc city and county students in media arts
notes: The foundation's own site carries the current date and the four streams; the copies of these criteria hosted on the school division's site are older and give a different deadline. Trust the foundation. Money is held in trust and released on proof of tuition or receipt, and it expires August 31, 2029.
description: One of four streams the Leduc Performing Arts and Cultural Foundation runs, each with two tiers. The scholarship pays up to $1,000 to a grade 12 student, or one who has finished Media Arts at the 10, 20 and 30 levels, and has to go toward post-secondary study, though continuing in media arts is explicitly not required. The award pays up to $500 to a student from grade 7 up and covers lessons, camps, workshops or equipment instead. You have to attend a City of Leduc or County of Leduc school and be 19 or under. The media submission is a portfolio of your electronic arts work, up to four minutes, sent by email with a teacher or mentor reference. The foundation exists as a legacy of Florence Mackenzie, a Black Gold teacher.
metaDetail: Judged on a portfolio of up to four minutes.

title: Leduc Performing Arts and Cultural Foundation Visual Arts Scholarship

The visual submission is files of your art sent by email against the foundation's art submission guidelines, with a teacher or mentor reference. The foundation exists as a legacy of Florence Mackenzie, a Black Gold teacher.
metaDetail: Judged on a portfolio, with a mentor reference.

title: Leduc Performing Arts and Cultural Foundation Music Arts Scholarship
audience: Leduc city and county students in music arts

Music is judged live: you perform two or three pieces at the MacLab Centre for Performing Arts, up to fifteen minutes including your introductions. The foundation exists as a legacy of Florence Mackenzie, a Black Gold teacher.
metaDetail: Judged by live performance at the MacLab Centre.

title: Leduc Performing Arts and Cultural Foundation Performing Arts Scholarship
audience: Leduc city and county students in performing arts
notes: The foundation's own site carries the current date and the four streams; the copies of these criteria hosted on the school division's site are older and give a different deadline. Trust the foundation. Money is held in trust and released on proof of tuition or receipt, and it expires August 31, 2029.
description: One of four streams the Leduc Performing Arts and Cultural Foundation runs, each with two tiers. The scholarship pays up to $1,000 to a grade 12 student, or one who has finished Performing Arts at the 10, 20 and 30 levels, and has to go toward post-secondary study, though continuing in performing arts is explicitly not required. The award pays up to $500 to a student from grade 7 up and covers lessons, camps, workshops or equipment instead. You have to attend a City of Leduc or County of Leduc school and be 19 or under. Performing arts is judged live at the MacLab Centre, up to fifteen minutes including your introduction, and theatre, storytelling, dance and singing all count. The foundation exists as a legacy of Florence Mackenzie, a Black Gold teacher.
metaDetail: Theatre, storytelling, dance and singing all count.

title: Bill Procyk Memorial Scholarship
audience: Fort High grade 12 students with 80% in a CTS course
notes: All of Fort High's internal awards ride on one checklist form filed with Student Services, and you tick every award you want on the same sheet and write how you meet each one. The date on the form is a bare June 1 with no year, so it repeats.
description: For a grade 12 Fort Saskatchewan High School student registered at a post-secondary institution who has achieved 80% or higher in a CTS course, with foods and fashion named alongside the rest of Career and Technology Studies. The mark is the only bar, so a strong shop or foods student with an ordinary academic transcript is exactly who this is written for.
metaDetail: Foods and fashion count as CTS here.

title: Fort Saskatchewan High School Community Leadership Award
audience: Fort High students in any grade who lead and volunteer
notes: All of Fort High's internal awards ride on one checklist form filed with Student Services, and you tick every award you want on the same sheet and write how you meet each one. The date on the form is a bare June 1 with no year, so it repeats.
description: Open to a Fort High student from any grade level, which makes it one of the few awards here a grade 10 can win. It is judged on active involvement in leadership activity at the school, community volunteering and service, and acting as an ambassador for both the school and the City of Fort Saskatchewan. Academic standing has to be satisfactory but is not otherwise scored.
metaDetail: Open from any grade, not just grade 12.

title: Fort Saskatchewan Community Hospital Auxiliary Bursary
audience: Fort High students entering a medical field
notes: All of Fort High's internal awards ride on one checklist form filed with Student Services, and you tick every award you want on the same sheet and write how you meet each one. The date on the form is a bare June 1 with no year, so it repeats.
description: Funded by the auxiliary of the Fort Saskatchewan Community Hospital for a student attending a post-secondary institution in a medical field. The criteria name nothing beyond the field itself, no average and no service record, so the pool is whoever in the graduating class is heading into medicine or an allied health programme.
metaDetail: Field of study is the whole criterion.

title: Fort Saskatchewan High School Opportunity Scholarship
audience: Fort High students with financial need and strong marks
notes: All of Fort High's internal awards ride on one checklist form filed with Student Services, and you tick every award you want on the same sheet and write how you meet each one. The date on the form is a bare June 1 with no year, so it repeats.
description: For a Fort High student in financial need who also has strong academic performance and will be attending a post-secondary institution. It sits between the school's two need-based awards and its academic ones by asking for both at once, so a strong transcript is not on its own enough and neither is need.
metaDetail: Weighs need and academic performance together.

title: Fort High Health Sciences Scholarship
audience: Fort High students entering a health sciences faculty
notes: All of Fort High's internal awards ride on one checklist form filed with Student Services, and you tick every award you want on the same sheet and write how you meet each one. The date on the form is a bare June 1 with no year, so it repeats.
description: For a strong academic Fort High student registered in a health sciences faculty at a post-secondary institution, with medicine, dentistry and X-ray technician given as examples of what counts. It overlaps with the hospital auxiliary bursary beside it, and since the school's application is a single checklist you tick both rather than choosing between them.
metaDetail: Wants a faculty placement, not just an interest.

title: Old Red Brick Fort High School Reunion Award
audience: Fort High students who worked hard without top marks
notes: All of Fort High's internal awards ride on one checklist form filed with Student Services, and you tick every award you want on the same sheet and write how you meet each one. The date on the form is a bare June 1 with no year, so it repeats.
description: Funded by the alumni of the old red brick Fort High and written for a student registered at a post-secondary institution who exemplified hard work without necessarily having top marks, has overcome some adversity, and is in financial need. All three parts of that are unusual to see stated so plainly, and together they describe a student most award criteria quietly exclude.
metaDetail: Says outright that top marks are not the point.

title: Fort High Perseverance and Dedication Award
audience: Fort High students with limited income and real dedication
notes: All of Fort High's internal awards ride on one checklist form filed with Student Services, and you tick every award you want on the same sheet and write how you meet each one. The date on the form is a bare June 1 with no year, so it repeats.
description: The criteria here go further than any other award on this list: the student must have a passing grade without regard for percentages, and limited income. Above all the award asks for dedication to studies and to the school. If your marks have kept you out of every other application, this is the one written with you in mind.
metaDetail: A passing grade is enough; percentages are ignored.

title: Royal Canadian Legion Ladies Auxiliary Leadership Award
audience: Fort High grade 12 students active in school life
notes: All of Fort High's internal awards ride on one checklist form filed with Student Services, and you tick every award you want on the same sheet and write how you meet each one. The date on the form is a bare June 1 with no year, so it repeats.
description: The Royal Canadian Legion Ladies Auxiliary in Fort Saskatchewan fund this for a grade 12 student who shows leadership and participation in school activities. Worth noting against Legion bursaries elsewhere in Alberta, which usually require descent from a veteran: this one asks only for the leadership and the participation.
metaDetail: No veteran descent required, unlike most Legion money.

title: Serge Lopushinsky Memorial Scholarship
audience: Fort High graduates from a farming family or with a passion for music
notes: All of Fort High's internal awards ride on one checklist form filed with Student Services, and you tick every award you want on the same sheet and write how you meet each one. The date on the form is a bare June 1 with no year, so it repeats.
description: For a graduating Fort High student continuing to post-secondary who either comes from a rural farming family or has a passion for music. The two routes are unrelated and it is an either-or, not a both, which doubles the number of students who can genuinely apply. The award also asks that you exemplify the qualities Fort High knew Serge for, described on the form as Sting Style.
metaDetail: Two unrelated routes in, and either one qualifies.

title: Victoria Lodge Number 13 Fellowship Award
audience: Fort High grade 12 students with school spirit and concern for peers
notes: All of Fort High's internal awards ride on one checklist form filed with Student Services, and you tick every award you want on the same sheet and write how you meet each one. The date on the form is a bare June 1 with no year, so it repeats.
description: Victoria Lodge Number 13 fund this for a grade 12 student who shows good school spirit, benevolence and concern for fellow peers, and active participation in school and community affairs. The middle criterion is the distinctive one: this is decided partly on how you treat the people around you, which is not something a transcript records.
metaDetail: Judged on how you treat other students.

title: Konica Minolta Award
audience: Elk Island students who overcame adversity to graduate
notes: Elk Island runs this through myBlueprint, so you need a division account to see the form at all. The date the division published was dated to 2026 rather than left as a repeating day, so treat the month as the guide and confirm the exact day with your counsellor.
description: Six Elk Island students are selected for this $500 award, which recognises students who have overcome some level of adversity to graduate and continue learning in any capacity. The last three words matter: the criteria cover students working toward an Alberta High School Certificate of Achievement as well as a Diploma, so it reaches students most graduation awards are closed to. It needs both a written student submission and a letter of support from the school.
metaDetail: Six awards, and a certificate of achievement qualifies.

title: WesTEC Scholarship
audience: Elk Island grade 12 students heading into STEM
notes: Elk Island runs this through myBlueprint, so you need a division account to see the form at all. The date the division published was dated to 2026 rather than left as a repeating day, so treat the month as the guide and confirm the exact day with your counsellor.
description: Dow Canada recognises two Elk Island students a year with $500 each for academic achievement and demonstrated innovation in science, technology, engineering and mathematics. Selection comes down to a 300-word abstract on a single prompt: describe a time you took an innovative approach to solving a problem that made a positive impact, including the problem, the challenges and the outcome. The prompt explicitly says the example does not have to be a STEM activity.
metaDetail: Decided on one 300-word abstract about innovation.

title: Bunzl Scholarship
audience: Elk Island students who can write about sustainability
notes: Elk Island runs this through myBlueprint, so you need a division account to see the form at all. The date the division published was dated to 2026 rather than left as a repeating day, so treat the month as the guide and confirm the exact day with your counsellor.
description: Five scholarships of $750 for Elk Island students, decided on a 500-word essay about sustainability. Suggested angles include why sustainability matters to you personally, how it shows up in your daily life or community, how sustainable thinking creates long term change, and how it connects to your studies or career. Marking weighs clarity and organisation, original thinking and personal insight, relevance, quality of writing, and use of supporting evidence, so this is a writing competition rather than a transcript one.
metaDetail: Five awards, decided on a 500-word essay.

title: Glen Hauk Memorial Keyera Scholarship
audience: Fort Saskatchewan and Sherwood Park students entering a trade or power engineering
notes: Elk Island runs this through myBlueprint, so you need a division account to see the form at all. The date the division published was dated to 2026 rather than left as a repeating day, so treat the month as the guide and confirm the exact day with your counsellor.
description: Keyera fund a single non-renewable $2,500 scholarship in memory of Glen Hauk for a student entering the first year of a Registered Apprenticeship Program in a qualifying trade, or an accredited full-time power engineering programme. You have to graduate from one of six named schools across Fort Saskatchewan and Sherwood Park. The committee is looking for commitment to the community, a motivated and positive attitude with a desire to improve, and a clear vision of your career goals. Power engineering is rarely named in scholarship criteria at all, which makes this worth knowing about.
metaDetail: Power engineering counts alongside a RAP trade.

title: Kevin Gaetz Scholarship
audience: Elk Island students whose finances would restrict post-secondary
notes: You cannot apply for this one; each Elk Island school nominates up to two students, so the useful move is telling a counsellor you want to be considered. Black Gold School Division runs a separate award from the same Edmonton Community Foundation fund with its own application and a June 30 date, so a student who moves between the divisions is looking at two different routes. Elk Island describes the payment only as a monetary amount and publishes no figure.
description: Paid from the Edmonton Community Foundation, with up to two students at each Elk Island high school receiving an amount to support post-secondary study. The award goes to a student who meets the entrance requirements for the programme to be supported and has financial need that would restrict their ability to pursue it, together with perseverance and commitment to post-secondary education, described in the criteria as the desire and determination to keep learning in an area of interest.
metaDetail: Nomination only, up to two students per school.

title: Twice But Nice Scholarship
audience: Any Fort Saskatchewan high school graduate, including gap year students
notes: The store publishes a dated cutoff each year; the 2026 round closed June 14, and the date shown here assumes the same day repeats, so confirm it on their site. Applications must be one combined PDF emailed in, with letters of reference on letterhead, a conditional acceptance letter and a transcript. Recipients attend the March annual general meeting to report back, and anyone who withdraws within 30 days of a term start has to repay.
description: A thrift store funds the two largest awards in Fort Saskatchewan: $5,000 each, with the Anne Springman Scholarship for a student going to college or university and the Lesley Macmillan Scholarship for one going to a technical institute, trade school or apprenticeship. If nobody applies on one side they may award both on the other. Financial need carries 30 of the 100 selection points, work experience 20, personal challenges 15, and marks only 10, and the criteria say plainly that grades matter only insofar as they got you accepted. Eligibility reaches homeschooled students, Fort Saskatchewan Outreach, Strathcona Christian Academy and students in designated programmes outside the city, and you may apply in your graduating year or within one year of it.
metaDetail: Two awards of $5,000, one reserved for trades.

title: Lion Don Westman Legacy Scholarship
audience: Fort Saskatchewan graduates from Fort High and St. André Bessette
notes: Applications close September 15, a bare repeating date rather than one tied to a year, and they go to the Lions club directly by email or post rather than through a school. That places it after graduation, when most students have stopped looking.
description: The Fort Saskatchewan Lions Club run this in memory of Lion Don Westman, and their published recipient lists show it going to students from Fort Saskatchewan High School and St. André Bessette Catholic High School in alternating pairs each year. The application is a downloadable form sent to the club, not something the school collects, so it is easy to miss entirely if you are relying on the school awards package.
metaDetail: Closes after graduation, in mid September.

title: NCIA Scholarship
audience: Industrial Heartland students entering engineering, trades or technology
notes: The association publishes recipients rather than criteria or a date, and Elk Island lists the application among its own, so the route in is your counsellor or myBlueprint. Recent recipients have come from Fort Saskatchewan and Sherwood Park schools.
description: The Northeast Capital Industrial Association is the industry body for Alberta's Industrial Heartland, headquartered in Fort Saskatchewan, and it awarded $2,000 to each of four students in its most recent round. Its recipients have been heading into electrical engineering, engineering at the University of Alberta, instrumentation engineering technology at NAIT and power engineering at NAIT, which tells you more about what wins it than any published rubric would: a concrete plan tied to industry in the region, in a degree or a diploma equally.
metaDetail: Four awards went out in the most recent round.

title: Andy Polanski Leader of Tomorrow Memorial Scholarship
audience: Fort Saskatchewan graduates who gave back to the community
notes: The foundation publishes no closing date on its scholarship page, so watch it through the spring or ask the foundation directly. Fort High lists it among its community scholarships, so a counsellor there will know the timing.
description: The Andy Polanski Charitable Foundation was established in 2014 after the death of Andy Polanski, a young man remembered for volunteering across his school and community. It offers $1,000 to a graduate of a Fort Saskatchewan high school going on to post-secondary who has demonstrated the importance of giving back and, through it, has had an impact on others. The foundation's own motto frames the criterion better than a rubric could: life is measured by the fingerprints you leave behind.
metaDetail: Judged on your impact on other people.

title: Footprints to your Future Scholarship
audience: Fort Saskatchewan students who completed high school requirements
notes: This runs alongside the foundation's Leader of Tomorrow award on the same page and in partnership with another organisation, and neither carries a published deadline, so ask the foundation or Fort High student services when it opens.
description: The second of the two Andy Polanski Legacy Scholarships, worth $1,000 to a Fort Saskatchewan high school student who has completed their high school requirements and is pursuing post-secondary education. It is run in partnership rather than by the foundation alone, and its criteria are written more broadly than its sibling award, which asks specifically about giving back.
metaDetail: The second of two Andy Polanski Legacy awards.

title: Josephburg Ag Society Scholarship
audience: Post-secondary students in any year, with no age limit
notes: The society published a dated cutoff of September 1, 2026 for its most recent round, which has now passed, and it has not yet posted the next one. No residency rule is stated anywhere in the criteria, so despite being a local society this is open well beyond Josephburg; it is listed on the Fort Saskatchewan hub because the schools there promote it.
description: The Josephburg Agricultural Society awards three $1,000 scholarships, judged equally on academic achievement and community involvement, with one reserved for a student in a programme leading to a career in agriculture and one given in memory of longtime director Doug Maschmeyer. The eligibility is unusually wide: any post-secondary student starting or already enrolled in any year of an accredited programme, degree or diploma, with no age limit, and you may win it up to three times. The application is a 500-word essay on what volunteerism means to you plus a video of no more than 90 seconds covering your community involvement, academics and career goals.
metaDetail: Three awards, and you can win it up to three times.

title: John M. Kerr Memorial Bursary
audience: 2SLGBTQIA+ students in any accredited Alberta post-secondary program
notes: The 2026 round is closed and recipients were announced at the court's coronation weekend in August, so the next intake opens in the new year. This is not a Fort Saskatchewan award, though Elk Island and Fort High both carry it on their lists; it is open across Alberta.
description: The Imperial Sovereign Court of the Wild Rose, an Edmonton charitable society that has been fundraising since 1976, grants these each year to students of the 2SLGBTQIA+ community entering any accredited post-secondary programme in Alberta. Bursaries are usually between $500 and $750, but the number and the amount both move with how much the court raises in a given year. The fund is managed by the court's own board of directors.
metaDetail: Amounts vary with what the court raises each year.

title: Chestermere High School Scholarship
audience: Chestermere High School graduates with 45 credits earned there
notes: Two rules here are worth more than the criteria. The deadline is September 1 of your graduating year, months after most school awards close, because it wants proof of registration rather than a letter of acceptance. And in a year when nobody applies, that year's graduates may apply the following year, which is a second chance almost no award offers. Forms come from the guidance office, usually updated in April.
description: Started in 1978 by a Chestermere student, Carolyn Tester, who noticed there was nothing for students who were capable of further study and willing to do it but did not have the marks to win the awards that existed. The fund was built by donation to a principal now sitting at $15,000, and the award is paid from the interest, so a committee of five community members and a school representative decides each year both who wins and how much they get. Selection weighs academic proficiency, extracurricular involvement, citizenship, leadership and financial need together.
metaDetail: Built for capable students without top marks.

title: Jaydon Sommerfeld Memorial Bursary
audience: Chestermere High School grade 12 students who played a sport
notes: Read the sports rule before you rule yourself out: intramurals count, and so do jiu jitsu, weight lifting and figure skating. The mark rule is stricter than it looks, though, because the 65 per cent has to hold in each grade twelve subject rather than on average. Applications are emailed to Mr. Bates at mbates@rockyview.ab.ca with the subject line the form specifies, and you are asked for a social insurance number.
description: In memory of Jaydon Sommerfeld, a Chestermere High student and lacrosse and hockey player who died in a car accident in June 2015 and whose organs went to six strangers. At least four bursaries of $500 are given every year. The criteria say plainly that this is not an academic award and the highest mark does not win it: the committee is looking for kindness, thoughtfulness, personal integrity, love of life and work ethic, the qualities Jaydon showed. The money can go to post-secondary costs or to anything else that gets you to gainful employment.
metaDetail: Intramurals count as the sports requirement.

title: Jim Cellars Memorial Welding Scholarship
audience: Chestermere High School students who completed FAB10, FAB20 and FAB30
notes: The school published a dated June 17, 2026 deadline for the last round and picks a new date each year, so there is no repeating date to carry and you should ask Mr. Dennis for this year's. Step one is a conversation rather than a form: you meet Mr. Dennis and Mr. Wiens first to check you are a strong candidate, then submit the letter. Expect an interview with Brian Cellars, and expect to attend the awards night in the fall, since he presents it in person.
description: A $1,000 award for a grade 12 Chestermere High student who has shown outstanding skill in Fabrication, named for Jim Cellars, a welder his family describe as an artist, inventor and engineer who taught the trade to many. Three things gate it: all three of FAB10, FAB20 and FAB30, proof you have applied to or enrolled in a post-secondary welding program, and a 150-word letter on why you are a strong candidate and how the money advances your career. The letter has to carry your social insurance number, so write it somewhere you can keep private.
metaDetail: All three Fabrication levels are required.

title: Calgary Black Chambers Cavalry FC Athletic Scholarship

description: Two awards of $5,000, paid straight to tuition, for Black Canadian citizens or permanent residents who are active student athletes on a varsity women's or men's team at a Calgary post-secondary institution. Any year of a full-time undergraduate degree or diploma qualifies, the bar is a cumulative GPA of 2.7 or 70 per cent, and one reference letter is required.
metaDetail: Varsity only, and one award each for women and men.

title: Calgary Black Chambers TransAlta STEM Scholarship

The application is a letter to the principal describing yourself and what you intend to study or do, and candidates who make the shortlist are interviewed by a selection committee at the school. Because it is awarded per school rather than per division, a small francophone school is a much better place to win it from than a large one.

audience: Battle River School Division graduates entering agriculture or a supporting field

title: Federation of Alberta Gas Co-ops Achievement Award
audience: Children of rural Alberta gas co-op members entering post-secondary
notes: The date is not a submission deadline in the usual sense: the form has to be signed by your local gas co-op, band, town, village or county office no later than October 1 following graduation, so the office you need is a third party with its own hours.
description: Four awards of $1,000 handed out at the FedGas annual general meeting to children of co-operative members of gas utilities in the federation, and to children of landowners serviced by member towns, villages, counties or First Nations. The membership must have been in place a full year, and at least 75% in core subjects is required rather than preferred. Preference goes to fields that apply to the natural gas industry, such as gas utility operator, gasfitter, pipefitter, power engineering and heavy equipment technician, or to rural-based programs.
metaDetail: 75% in core subjects is a hard floor, not a preference.
